records.name: Alleles, zygosity and copy state
records.tldr: An allele is a sequence version at a genomic location. Which versions are present and how many DNA copies exist are separate questions.
records.summary: At a diploid location, heterozygous means that the two copies differ in the feature being considered; homozygous means they match. Hemizygous describes a single copy in the specified context. Tumor gains, losses and genome doubling can make a two-copy model inadequate. Loss of heterozygosity means loss of previously different allelic information; it can accompany a deletion or occur while total copy count remains unchanged. Total copy number alone cannot identify which allele was retained.

Purity, local copy state, subclonal mixtures and method affect it; it is not directly a cancer-cell percentage or a zygosity call. Phase asks whether specified variants share a DNA copy, a further question that a gene-name match does not answer.

Biallelic inactivation concerns whether either parental contribution still supplies useful function in the relevant cancer-cell population, rather than simply counting two physical DNA copies or two events somewhere in a tissue. A damaging change plus loss of the other contribution can support it, but phasing, allele-specific copy state, consequence and cell mixture matter. High VAF alone cannot establish this state. Nguyen and colleagues' pan-cancer analysis associated particular biallelic repair-gene alterations with genomic damage patterns; that association does not make every variant in every repair gene functionally equivalent or establish present drug sensitivity.

records.name: Apoptosis
records.tldr: Apoptosis is a regulated process that dismantles a cell. Whether the dying cell stimulates protective immunity is a separate question.
records.summary: The mitochondrial route uses BCL-2-family control of BAX and BAK and cytochrome c release. In cell experiments, combined BAX and BAK loss blocked mitochondrial responses to several apoptotic stimuli; this does not establish resistance to all forms of death. Death-receptor signals provide another route. Apoptosis is not inherently immune-silent: anthracycline-treated tumour cells showed calreticulin-dependent immunogenicity in mouse experiments. A death marker, a mitochondrial response and sustained killing answer different questions. Protein abundance alone cannot establish dependence or choose a treatment.

notes: Intrinsic apoptosis involves mitochondrial outer-membrane permeabilisation, cytochrome c release into the cytosol, apoptosome assembly and caspase-9 activation upstream of executioner caspases such as caspase-3 and caspase-7. Death-receptor signalling can activate caspase-8; BID cleavage links this route to mitochondria. Initiator and executioner roles differ.

The BCL-2 family contains survival proteins, including BCL-2, BCL-XL and MCL-1; BH3-only stress mediators, including BIM, BID and PUMA; and pore-forming effectors BAX and BAK. In experimental cells, loss of both BAX and BAK blocked several mitochondrial apoptotic responses, rather than every possible form of death.

Cytochrome c moves from the mitochondrial intermembrane compartment, including crista stores, across the outer membrane to the cytosol. It does not begin in the matrix. The inner membrane separates these compartments; the spatial sketch is simplified, with no implied pore stoichiometry.

A stain for BCL-XL measures abundance rather than survival dependence. BCL2 and BCL2L1 are different genes, and inhibitor selectivity matters. Souers and colleagues re-engineered dual BCL-2/BCL-XL inhibition into BCL-2-selective ABT-199, sparing human platelets; early tumour lysis in three refractory chronic lymphocytic leukaemia patients does not establish benefit in every tumour. A mitochondrial response, caspase marker, sustained killing and immune protection remain separate outcomes. Keep cell identity, timing, handling controls and later survival or regrowth with cleaved-caspase assays, membrane readouts and microscopy. Mitochondrial BH3 challenges test readiness under a defined protocol, rather than completed killing or clinical benefit.

Compare mechanism, morphology, immune consequence and living arrest separately. Apoptosis uses regulated dismantling; necrotic morphology describes boundary failure; ferroptosis requires iron-dependent lipid damage causing death; immunogenicity requires a compatible adaptive response; senescence is a living arrest. These categories are not mutually exclusive outcomes or a universal appearance-based classifier.

In the fictional killing experiment, rescue by both an iron chelator and a lipid-protecting compound with no caspase-inhibitor rescue supports a ferroptosis hypothesis. Check lipid damage, death timing, perturbation specificity and GPX4 or glutathione-related mechanisms before attribution; immunogenicity is a separate test. A single stain is not enough.

records.name: Autophagy
records.tldr: Autophagy delivers cellular material for breakdown and reuse. The amount present, the rate of recycling and whether cells need it to survive are different questions.
records.summary: Macroautophagy encloses cargo in autophagosomes for lysosomal delivery and breakdown. LC3 abundance alone cannot distinguish increased formation from reduced removal. Tandem fluorescent LC3 reporters exploit different responses to acidic and degradative conditions to examine maturation in cell experiments; interpretation requires appropriate controls. Flux and survival dependence need separate tests. In a randomised phase 2 trial of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. A drug trial does not by itself establish selective autophagy dependence in a tumour.

notes: Leading programmes: Amaravadi (Penn) on autophagy inhibition trials; Kimmelman (NYU) on PDAC autophagy and MHC-I; Der (UNC) on KRAS/autophagy.

Macroautophagy encloses cargo in a double-membrane autophagosome, delivers it through lysosomal fusion and degrades it for reuse. Formation, delivery and breakdown are separate steps; not all lysosomal processes use autophagosomes. Active recycling often supports stress adaptation, whereas autophagy-dependent death requires causal evidence implicating the machinery.

A completed macroautophagosome has separate inner and outer membranes, with space between them. When it fuses with a lysosome, the outer membrane joins the lysosomal boundary, while the inner membrane is degraded before enzymes gain access to the enclosed cargo. Itakura and colleagues located syntaxin 17 on completed autophagosomes, and Tsuboyama and colleagues found that loss of ATG conjugation systems markedly delayed inner-membrane degradation even when fusion occurred. A direct-fusion sketch omits intermediate endosomal interactions described in multicellular organisms; it is not the complete route taken by every compartment.

Product return has evidence in defined systems. In leucine-starved cultured human HEK-293T cells, Wyant and colleagues found that SLC38A9 was needed for leucine made by lysosomal protein breakdown to reach the cytosol; the response also depended on the autophagy protein ATG7. Abu-Remaileh and colleagues measured regulated lysosomal amino-acid exchange in mammalian cells. Yeast experiments identified Atg22, Avt3 and Avt4 as partially redundant vacuolar amino-acid exporters. These results support amino-acid recycling in those systems, without establishing transport of every breakdown product, secretion from the cell or guaranteed growth.

More lipidated LC3-II can reflect greater formation or slower removal. A controlled short lysosomal block and complementary tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter can help examine turnover and delivery to acidic compartments. Equal starting amounts can have different later fates. Little additional accumulation can reflect a late block, low formation or an unsuitable window; it does not establish dependence.

Flux, selected-cargo clearance and survival dependence are different claims. NBR1 experiments identify selective ubiquitinated-cargo handling, not a universal LC3 cargo census. Use time courses, viable-cell normalisation, verified lysosomal inhibition and independent perturbations; autophagy proteins can have other functions. Lower mTOR signalling can change initiation without guaranteeing completed degradation. Typical research outputs include normalised LC3-II band intensity, reporter compartments per cell and selected-cargo disappearance over time. Tested cultures are consumed or perturbed, and prolonged lysosomal inhibition can itself disturb the system. No universal LC3 or flux cutoff selects treatment.

In Karasic and colleagues' randomised phase 2 study of 112 people with advanced pancreatic cancer, adding hydroxychloroquine to gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel increased response rate but did not improve the primary endpoint of survival at 12 months. Response was 38.2% versus 21.1%; 12-month survival was 41% versus 49%. These group results do not show selective autophagy dependence or recommend this combination.

Klionsky's 2021 assay guidelines distinguish LC3 carrier flux from actual cargo or substrate flux. LC3-II is the lipid-attached form of microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; accumulation can reflect formation or slower removal. Compare treatment alone, a verified lysosomal block such as bafilomycin A1 alone, both together and the relevant baseline, with suitable time and dose windows. An additional LC3-II increase can support turnover under those conditions, but partial inhibition, saturation, low formation or cell death can complicate the comparison. Little change is not a unique diagnosis of an existing late block. A tandem two-colour reporter adds information about acidic delivery, not proof that every cargo completed degradation. Pair markers with an appropriate cargo measurement. Sequestosome 1, SQSTM1/p62, is an adaptor whose abundance also depends on expression and other processes, so one p62 snapshot cannot establish blockage.

A fictional one-hour recycling-station comparison starts with 20 waiting bags in each station. A receives 30 and processes 30, leaving 20; B receives five and processes none, leaving 25. Equal initial piles, including a six-bag schematic snapshot, cannot identify the rate or the later outcome. Bags are not LC3 molecules or assay thresholds: real markers are produced and removed, cargos differ, and a perturbation can affect several steps. Measure completion over time with appropriate controls. Even verified flow does not establish survival dependence; after a specific perturbation, more death can support a protective role, less drug-induced death can support a contribution to that death response, and changed flow with similar survival leaves timing or compensation as possible limits.

Breast-cancer studies illustrate the conditional direction. Bellare 2021 reported that genetic disruption or chloroquine increased talazoparib sensitivity in the tested HR-proficient cells and xenografts. Arun 2015 found that ATG5 reduction partly reduced olaparib-induced apoptosis in BRCA2-mutant HCC-1428 cells, an oestrogen-receptor-positive line rather than a triple-negative model. These different drugs, models and perturbations do not define one protective or death-promoting label for all tumours. Bellare's 2025 correction replaced representative MCF7 images in Figure 5c as well as a liver-histology image in Figure 6f. The authors stated that replicate-based quantification and interpretation were unchanged; that statement is theirs, not an independent validation of the replacement images.

Bulk RNA abundance measures messages across the sampled cell mixture; it does not time cargo flow or establish dependence. ATG13 and FIP200 participate with ULK1 in initiation machinery, as Ganley 2009 studied, but an alteration in a component does not establish the direction of completed recycling. A mechanistic dependence test should measure the proposed change before extensive death alters the markers, combine complementary readouts, and where feasible perturb more than one autophagy gene at different steps. Klionsky's guidelines also caution that these proteins have other functions. Restoration and independent perturbations strengthen a specific causal explanation without making every genetic manipulation perfectly selective. A lower ATP or metabolic signal alone is neither counted death nor proof of autophagy dependence.
records.analogy: A besieged city that starts recycling furniture into firewood. It keeps the lights on through the siege, and burning the 'wanted posters' (MHC) hides its criminals too.
interventions: Clinical drug studies and mechanistic dependence tests answer different questions.
Assess flux, selected cargo and survival separately with complementary controls.

records.name: BRCA reversion mutations
records.tldr: A secondary change in a tumour can sometimes restore BRCA repair function and contribute to treatment resistance. A DNA prediction and demonstrated repair function are different findings.
records.summary: Some tumours acquire secondary BRCA changes that restore a disrupted reading frame or enable production of functional repair protein. Such changes can contribute to resistance to platinum compounds and PARP inhibitors. A sequence-based prediction, a measured protein and demonstrated repair function are different levels of evidence; a restored frame alone does not establish a patient's drug response.

notes: Sakai 2008 described secondary BRCA2 changes that restored the reading frame in breast and pancreatic cancer models. The selected clones resisted cisplatin and the experimental PARP inhibitor AG14361. A recurrent BRCA2-mutated ovarian tumour with acquired cisplatin resistance also carried a reversion. These examples establish a possible resistance mechanism, rather than a universal frequency across cancers, assays or medicines.

Sakai 2009 studied ovarian cancer cell lines from one BRCA2-variant carrier. A secondary change cancelled an inherited nonsense variant, BRCA2 protein was detectable in resistant lines, and further experiments selected BRCA2-restored clones. Reducing BRCA2 with siRNA made the restored clones and PEO4 cells more sensitive to cisplatin and AG14361. This is evidence from a named cellular model and depletion experiment, rather than a clinical trial selecting a subsequent treatment.

Reading rule: these experiments do not supply a general incidence percentage or a treatment-switch rule. A reversion-negative result does not by itself show that every resistance mechanism is absent or establish benefit from another course of a PARP inhibitor. Interpretation needs the tested sequence regions, sample, assay limits and relevant clinical evidence. An inherited variant and a secondary tumour variant remain separate findings.

A reading frame groups the DNA sequence into three-letter instructions. A missing letter can change the groups that follow; a nearby second edit can restore the grouping without recreating the original sequence. In a fictional tumour with a two-base BRCA1 deletion, a further one-base deletion on the same altered copy gives a net three-base loss. Two plus six gives eight and does not restore the original frame. The positions, affected copy and intervening sequence still matter. Even after a response lasting a year, this sequence calculation supplies a candidate explanation for later resistance, not proof of protein function or treatment causation.

An inherited BRCA variant does not by itself establish loss of both working copies in a tumour. The functional state of the remaining copy matters. A restoring change can expand under treatment selection, whether it arose earlier or later; detecting it at progression does not date its origin or show that treatment deliberately produced it. A secondary tumour change also does not invalidate the original variant call or remove the inherited variant from the person's other cells. Blood contains a mixture of tumour and non-tumour DNA, so linking changes to the same copy can be important.

Alongside Sakai's 2008 experiments, Edwards 2008 selected PARP-inhibitor-resistant CAPAN1 pancreatic cancer cells whose intragenic BRCA2 deletions restored an open reading frame. The authors reported restored repair-related findings and similar secondary changes in carboplatin-resistant ovarian tumours. This shows a possible route to cross-resistance in the tested systems, rather than a rule for every drug or tumour. Short matching sequences around some deletion junctions suggested an end-joining process; such a junction does not identify one responsible enzyme.

A restoring event can produce a shorter, partly functional protein. Nesic 2024 studied BRCA1 exon-11 frameshift ovarian and breast cancer models, including a matched before/after PARP-inhibitor pair, and reported secondary splice-site changes that increased shorter BRCA1 isoforms. Post-treatment ovarian cancer data also showed enrichment of these changes. These were hypomorphic proteins with partial function, not evidence that every splice change recreates normal full-length BRCA1 or produces the same drug response.

Reversion percentages depend on whom and what was counted. Tobalina's 2021 meta-analysis assembled 327 published patient cases after platinum or PARP-inhibitor progression: 234 ovarian, 27 breast, 13 pancreatic, 11 prostate and 42 of unspecified origin. It catalogued 269 reversion events in 86 people, about 26 per cent of these selected cases. Pettitt's 2020 catalogue contained more than 300 reversion events, with most deletions smaller than 100 bases; events are not independent patients. Among 283 sequence-informative events, 159 had microhomology-associated deletions. The net coding change must compensate for the original frameshift: a secondary deletion divisible by three does not by itself repair an earlier two-base loss. Exact wild-type restoration is one route, but mixed normal DNA and difficulty linking variants can hide it, so catalogue rarity does not establish its biological incidence.

Lin 2019 examined circulating tumour DNA before rucaparib in BRCA-mutated high-grade ovarian cancer. Reversions were detected in 2 of 11 platinum-refractory, 5 of 38 platinum-resistant and 1 of 48 platinum-sensitive cases. Median progression-free survival was 9.0 months without a detected pretreatment reversion versus 1.8 months with one, with a hazard ratio of 0.12 for the former versus the latter. These are associations within a selected treatment cohort, not a general population frequency or a randomised comparison of treatment choices. A negative result is limited by what the blood sample and assay could detect.

Weigelt 2017 sequenced blood from 19 germline-BRCA carriers with platinum-refractory or resistant ovarian cancer and five with pretreated metastatic breast cancer. Putative reversions were found in 4 of 19 ovarian cases, about 21 per cent, and 2 of 5 breast cases. Several changes could coexist, and functional experiments tested a subset. These small selected groups do not establish the frequency in all breast or ovarian cancers. One tissue biopsy samples one site; plasma can reveal changes shed by several sites while missing populations that shed little DNA or fall outside assay coverage.

Waks 2020 studied paired samples from eight selected BRCA1/2-mutant metastatic breast cancers that acquired platinum or PARP-inhibitor resistance. Four had definite or putative reversions and acquired RAD51 foci. Two other cases suggested repair-restoring routes: one had biallelic 53BP1 loss, with insufficient tissue for the protein or RAD51 assay; another had MRE11A amplification, increased RNA, DNA-end-processing findings and reacquired RAD51 foci. The proposed causal explanations have different amounts of direct evidence. Six patients acquired RAD51 foci overall; three subsequently received another platinum or PARP treatment and all three were resistant. This small selected cohort cannot establish a universal predictive rule.

Sequencing and functional testing answer different questions. A tissue or plasma assay needs coverage around the original variant, suitable deletion and splice-change detection, and a way to assess whether the changes share an allele; a hotspot-only panel can miss such events. RNA, protein or functional work may be needed for a proposed splice rescue. In Waks's RAD51 method, more than three nuclear foci in at least one cell across three examined fields supported repair proficiency, with geminin and control samples used for interpretation. A negative-foci sample with too few proliferating cells was uninterpretable. A visible focus alone does not establish completed repair, and a single RAD51 method cannot substitute for all sequence and clinical evidence.

Returning to the fictional two-plus-one deletion, neither a new scar score nor a functional result has actually been supplied. Restoring a gene does not by itself undo the chromosome alterations accumulated earlier, so historical scars can coexist with changed repair. It is reasonable to investigate a restoring protein and current RAD51 behaviour, but it is not reasonable to invent those measurements or predict an unchanged numerical score. End-joining and polymerase-theta inhibition are research directions for particular repair states; preventing future reversions or delaying resistance in people remains a hypothesis, rather than an established treatment consequence of this example.

records.name: Central dogma and molecular information flow
records.tldr: DNA copying, making RNA and making a protein are different processes. Following the route helps identify what each molecular test actually measured.
records.summary: Replication makes DNA from DNA. Transcription uses a DNA template to make RNA. Translation reads the coding sequence of a message in three-base codons to build a polypeptide; the transcript and reading frame matter. Functional noncoding RNAs do not need to become protein. Reverse transcription copies RNA into DNA in relevant viral and retrotransposon contexts. This information-flow map is not a guarantee that every DNA change produces a measured RNA or protein change.

notes: RNA processing, translation, folding, modification, localization and turnover can alter the path from a coding sequence to a functional product. records.name: Controlled perturbation experiment
records.tldr: A controlled perturbation changes one defined factor in an experiment and compares the response with control conditions, so that the change can be told apart from background, carrier effects and assay failure.
records.summary: A controlled perturbation deliberately changes a defined factor and measures the response against appropriate comparison conditions. Vehicle, positive, negative and mechanism controls answer different questions. A reproducible response can support an experimental claim without establishing its proposed mechanism or patient benefit. Baseline growth, timing, dose and the actual unit assigned to treatment matter.

notes: A vehicle control contains the carrier without the active treatment; an untreated condition asks a different question if the carrier has effects. A positive control checks that the assay can detect a known relevant response, while a negative or non-targeting control estimates background under its design. Another independent way to disrupt the same function can support a mechanism, and a rescue restores a function to test whether that reverses the response here. Off-target effects, incomplete restoration and model context limit interpretation. These are questions for matched model, timing and readout; no one control proves specificity or patient benefit, and agreement between similar readouts is not automatically independent mechanistic confirmation.

Keep what changed, the comparator, concentration or dose range, timing, assignment, readout and units, sample identities, replicate structure and variability. Repeated wells address variation under their preparation and allocation; independently obtained biological samples address another source of variation. Many wells from one tumour do not become independent patients, and repetition or a small p-value does not repair a missing comparison. A two-drug experiment needs vehicle, both single drugs and the combination. A larger combination effect than either single drug is not automatically synergy; that claim needs a stated reference model.

Fictional direct counts: vehicle-treated cells increase from 100 to 200 while drug-treated cells remain at 100. The endpoint drug count is half the vehicle count without measured net decline from the starting count, so calling it 50 per cent killing overstates the observation. Slower growth, death and a molecular change require their own readouts; direct death or recovery measurements could address further questions. Hafner and colleagues showed that conventional IC50 and maximal-effect measures depend on cell divisions during an assay and developed growth-rate metrics to address that dependence. A real experimental response does not by itself establish the responsible target or clinical benefit.

A fictional two-drug table normalises remaining viability to vehicle at 100 per cent: A leaves 70, B leaves 80, and combination examples leave 56 or 30. Highest single agent uses the better single-drug effect, a 70 per cent remaining-viability reference here. Bliss independence predicts 0.70 times 0.80 = 0.56, or 56 per cent. Both combinations exceed the HSA effect; 56 matches Bliss while 30 exceeds it at that dose pair. A further combination leaving 65 exceeds HSA but not Bliss. Loewe additivity instead needs equivalent-dose information from suitable individual dose-response curves; this one-point table cannot establish it. Report the model, dose-pair pattern, uncertainty and schedule. Interaction relative to a reference does not identify a biological mechanism, tolerable human exposure or a treatment choice.

A rescue restores a proposed missing function or supply and tests whether a defined effect reverses. Adding a cake mix back after its removal implicates the mixture without identifying flour, sugar or another ingredient; likewise, broad mevalonate add-back does not isolate cholesterol. More specific branch perturbations and appropriate add-backs can narrow the explanation. Partial rescue can reflect incomplete delivery or restoration as well as additional contributors, so it does not prove a second cause. Place the add-back relative to the blocked step: supplying GGPP after an upstream synthesis block is different from inhibiting the transferase that uses GGPP, which the added substrate cannot simply be assumed to bypass. Include restoration-only and matched controls, verify the restored process and distinguish growth, morphology and death. A genetic perturbation also has its own specificity limits.

Attribute each readout to the relevant cells. An ATP-based signal can change through cell number or per-cell metabolism, and slower single-cell mass accumulation does not by itself show death. Direct death measurements and regrowth after washout ask further questions; regrowth concerns surviving cells, not revival of cells already dead. A mixed culture can change composition, and a nonmalignant-cell label alone does not establish a validated healthy-tissue control. Ladan's breast-slice chemotherapy assay was compared with response during preoperative treatment in a defined setting. That assay-specific validation does not validate every postoperative combination, human exposure or clinical decision. An inadequate viable preparation should remain uninterpretable rather than be called resistant.

records.name: DNA
records.tldr: DNA stores sequence information. Its packaging, copying and use as a template for RNA are different processes.
records.summary: DNA contains nucleotide chains with a sugar–phosphate backbone and the bases A, T, C and G. Complementary A–T and C–G pairing joins antiparallel strands. Nuclear chromosomes contain DNA associated with proteins as chromatin; nucleosomes organize DNA around histones. Mitochondria carry a separate genome. A gene is a functional region within DNA, rather than an entire chromosome. Replication copies DNA, while transcription produces RNA from a selected template. Packaging and gene presence do not establish active transcription or a functional protein.

Experimental work also shows that this signal is not an unambiguous count of double-strand breaks. A sequencing variant call, a lesion assay and a damage-response stain answer different questions; one is not a count of the others.

records.name: Driver mutation
records.tldr: A driver alteration can promote tumour development in the context studied. That role does not by itself establish benefit from a drug.
records.summary:
A driver alteration contributes to cancer development in a specified biological context. Vogelstein and colleagues' 2013 review distinguished mutations conferring a selective growth advantage from passengers without that advantage. Calling a sequence change reliably does not establish which role it has, and a familiar gene can contain alterations with different or uncertain effects.

Contribution to cancer development, current survival dependence and clinical actionability are different claims. The SHIVA randomised study did not establish superior progression-free survival for its particular pathway-matching strategy in refractory advanced cancer; that result limits the tested strategy without invalidating every precision treatment. Specify the alteration, measured function, disease and treatment setting, intervention, comparator and outcome before concluding that a drug will help.

records.name: Endoplasmic reticulum stress and the unfolded protein response
records.tldr: Cells respond to strain on protein folding through several signalling branches. A response does not by itself establish cell death.
records.summary: The unfolded protein response has distinct outputs. IRE1-dependent processing of XBP1 RNA produces a potent transcriptional regulator; total XBP1 message and its spliced fraction are different measurements. PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and can reduce translation initiation. ER stress also promotes ATF6 proteolysis, releasing a fragment that acts in the nucleus. These findings come from molecular and cell experiments. Branch activity, adaptation, survival dependence and treatment benefit require separate evidence. Specify branch, timing, total protein or RNA controls and direct growth and death measurements.

notes: ER stress is an imbalance between protein-folding demand and local capacity; the unfolded protein response is an adaptation programme, not the same thing as the stress. IRE1 processes XBP1 RNA, PERK phosphorylates eIF2alpha and ATF6 processing releases a nuclear regulator. Distinct branches can alter folding capacity, incoming translation and disposal.

ATF6 travels from ER to Golgi for processing; the released fragment, rather than the intact membrane-bound precursor, acts in the nucleus. Total XBP1 RNA differs from its splice-form fraction. Other kinases can phosphorylate eIF2alpha, so one phosphosite cannot identify the whole response.

Specify preserved material, RNA quality, isoform-specific methods, total-protein controls, timing and identified cell populations. Splice-form fractions, processed ATF6 and defined phosphoprotein signals are different outputs. Increased XBP1 splicing with stable viable-cell counts supports a branch response, not lethal stress; measure growth and death directly and test causality independently. RNA or protein preparations and compatible tissue stains use material; functional dependence tests require viable cells. Report splice-form fractions, defined phosphosite signals or processed fragments with assay-specific controls, rather than a universal UPR-positive treatment threshold.

XBP1 depletion altered tumour growth and relapse in defined triple-negative breast cancer models, with an HIF1alpha transcriptional interaction. Model findings and patient expression-signature associations do not establish universal XBP1 dependence, an assay cutoff or a treatment benefit. Successful stress adaptation can support survival.

records.name: Ex vivo tumour fragments and slices
records.tldr: Living tumour pieces can retain local cells and architecture for a defined experiment outside the body, while losing circulating supply and recruitment.
records.summary: Fragment and slice preparations retain selected native tissue relationships rather than expanding a selected culture. Composition and function change with sampling, cutting, diffusion, medium and time. A retained vessel does not demonstrate perfusion, and visible immune cells do not establish the required interaction. Ladan's breast-slice assay and Salmon's human lung-slice migration experiments support different questions; neither validates every fragment test or treatment decision.

notes: Preparation and assay card. Input: suitable viable tissue with donor/site/time, collection and transport conditions, dimensions and culture window. Cutting, quality checks and endpoints consume finite material and limit available conditions. Compare baseline quality and untreated or carrier controls with defined exposures. Attribute counts, stain fractions, movement or metabolic signal to the relevant cells, with units, time and denominator. Thresholds are method-specific rather than a universal fragment score. Fragment names the preparation; a drug screen names an experiment it may support. Different pieces from one tumour can contain different populations, so matched treatments still need composition checks.

Primary preparation example. Ladan used 300 micrometre slices and three-day exposure in a defined anthracycline-based assay, measuring morphology, proliferation and apoptosis. Diffusion into slices differs from vascular delivery; host metabolic activation, clearance, organ toxicity and new immune recruitment were not recreated. Preparation injury, poor viability, uneven diffusion, changing populations and non-tumour signal can invalidate interpretation. A failed culture is not evidence of clinical resistance. Contamination is another reason for assay failure; short-term response does not establish durable elimination, systemic safety or benefit.

Endpoint and validation example. Ladan reported 23 usable assays among 30 tumour-containing biopsies; three of the 23 did not proceed to the clinical treatment comparison, leaving 20 evaluable patients and 15 concordant MRI comparisons. The agreement compared sensitive, intermediate and resistant categories after four courses of anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; it is not a binary drug-killing rate. The study did not observe an ex vivo resistant group, limiting assessment of resistance detection. Those denominators, assay version and preoperative setting cannot validate another postoperative choice. Salmon measured matrix-associated T-cell location and movement in viable lung-tumour slices, not treatment-selection benefit.

Fictional reading exercise. Two fragments with different starting malignant-cell fractions both lose total metabolic signal. Equal tumour killing has not been shown. Verify composition and an attributed death endpoint against controls. Retained neighbours can be useful for an immune question only when their viability and relevant function are demonstrated.
records.principle: Maintain viable tissue pieces for a defined comparison while measuring retained populations, quality and an attributed response.

records.name: Expanded access (compassionate use)
records.tldr: Expanded access permits qualifying treatment use of an investigational drug outside a clinical trial. Supply, physician responsibility and applicable regulatory and ethics requirements still need to be met.
records.summary: United States, federal regulation: drug and biologic expanded access has individual-patient, intermediate-population and widespread-treatment arrangements. Criteria include serious or immediately life-threatening illness, no comparable satisfactory alternative, justified potential benefit and risk, and no interference with clinical development. A new individual-patient IND is different from a protocol under an existing active IND. Supplier agreement and applicable FDA, ethics-review and consent requirements remain separate from manufacture, institutional readiness and scheduling. Access authorization is not evidence that treatment improves outcomes.

An individual-patient protocol under an existing active IND has no automatic 30-day wait, but must be submitted and have applicable IRB approval and consent. Widespread-use treatment protocols have different start rules.

Emergency individual-patient use can receive prior FDA authorisation by telephone or other rapid communication, allowing use to begin before the written expanded-access submission. That submission is due within 15 working days of FDA authorisation. When there is insufficient time for prospective institutional review board (IRB) review, report the emergency use to the IRB within 5 working days of starting treatment. Subsequent use at the same institution normally requires prior IRB review. FDA's April 2026 guidance also describes discretion for a subsequent emergency request when prior review is infeasible, with the same 5-working-day reporting requirement. This is not continuing permission or a promised treatment date.

A licensed physician acting as sponsor-investigator can use Form FDA 3926 for an individual-patient expanded-access IND in a non-emergency or emergency setting. Forms FDA 1571 and 1572 remain an alternative. FDA also lists eRequest for non-emergency individual-patient requests. The streamlined form is not a marketing application, a form for group requests or the device-access process.

When an application references another sponsor’s IND, a letter of authorization permits FDA to reference specified product information. That permission does not itself authorize treatment or guarantee drug supply. If such a letter is unavailable, the FDA review division can advise which other information may satisfy the applicable requirements.

For an unapproved investigational drug supplied under an IND, the IND sponsor needs separate prior written FDA authorization to charge for the drug. Recoverable costs and other conditions differ between clinical trials and expanded access. Treatment authorization does not itself authorize charging, and permission to recover drug costs does not decide insurer payment or the total cost of clinical care.

A reported FDA authorization rate needs its stated submitted-request denominator, period and request categories. It does not measure the fraction of everyone seeking the drug who obtains manufacturer supply, meets every requirement or actually receives treatment. An application authorization is not a personal probability of access or benefit.

For individual-patient expanded access, authorised drug-cost recovery is limited to direct costs attributable specifically to supplying the drug for that authorised investigational use. Examples include per-unit manufacture or acquisition, shipping and storage. Commercial-scale facilities and equipment, and research, administrative or labour expenses that would occur anyway, are indirect costs excluded by 21 CFR 312.8(d)(1). This concerns the sponsor's authorised drug charge, not every bill for clinical care.

For intermediate-size populations and treatment INDs or protocols under 21 CFR 312.315 and 312.320, the regulation additionally permits specified monitoring, IND reporting and directly associated administrative costs. Those additional categories do not apply automatically to an individual-patient arrangement. FDA authorisation of the treatment and prior written permission to charge remain separate.

FDA's request-forms page reports that, on average, 99% of expanded-access requests may proceed. That is the page's submitted-request statement, without a period specified there, not the fraction of everyone seeking a drug who receives it or benefits. Manufacturer agreement is an independent supply gate, and Project Facilitate is an FDA oncology point of contact that helps clinicians navigate requests. The reported FDA fraction does not measure how often supply is the limiting step or rank the obstacles in a particular plan.

The charging calculation required by 21 CFR 312.8(d)(3) must have supporting documentation and a statement that an independent certified public accountant reviewed and approved it. Expanded-access permission to charge normally lasts one year from FDA authorisation, or less if FDA specifies; the sponsor can request reauthorisation. FDA must withdraw permission if charging interferes with development or its authorisation criteria cease to be met. A two-year-old letter therefore needs a current reauthorisation check. These rules concern the investigational drug charge, not a promise of free clinical care.

Build a readiness record around the actual product, formulation, dose, route and schedule, its clinical rationale and alternatives, and the supporting quality, exposure and safety information. Name the sponsor and treating clinician, supplier and receiving or storage team, administering service, urgent-care destination, and people responsible for response assessment, toxicity management and reporting. Record the applicable submissions, review and consent, usable supply, costs, dependencies and possible stop conditions. Mark each answer confirmed, proposed or unknown with its responsible person and date; a checklist does not determine a patient's status. The treating team must assess suitability before administration; a laboratory result supplies neither eligibility nor a safe regimen. This checklist concerns U.S. drugs and biologics; device access, other countries and institutional rules can differ.

In a fictional request, a supplier says manufacture could finish next week while institutional review, the treatment plan and monitoring remain unresolved. That is a manufacturing estimate, not a treatment date. Similarly, FDA permission without a service able to administer and monitor the product leaves a delivery gate open. Ask which milestones are complete and which depend on others. A fictional new non-emergency individual-patient IND with supplier agreement, the necessary product information, applicable IRB review and consent can proceed when effective, ordinarily 30 days after FDA receipt or earlier FDA notice, provided it is not on hold. Supplier review, manufacture, FDA review, institutional review, shipping and scheduling each need their own estimate and dependencies.

For non-emergency individual-patient use, a physician using Form FDA 3926 may request the permitted institutional review board (IRB) chairperson or designated-member concurrence procedure instead of review at a convened full-board meeting. Concurrence must precede treatment under that procedure. It is not a waiver of informed consent: obtain the applicable written consent on an IRB-approved form. The supplier's letter of authorisation lets FDA reference specified information and does not replace these steps or FDA permission to proceed.

records.name: Ferroptosis & regulated cell death
records.tldr: Ferroptosis is a form of cell death involving iron-dependent membrane-lipid damage. General oxidative stress or one positive marker does not establish this mechanism.
records.summary: Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation and death. Cystine uptake through system xc- can support cysteine and glutathione availability; it does not transport glutathione itself. GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides, while FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q-associated defence. Dependence on these routes varies with the model and cellular conditions. Establishing the mechanism requires appropriately controlled measurements of death, lipid damage, iron dependence and rescue, with complementary perturbations. Findings in persistent or mesenchymal model cells do not establish a universal vulnerability or a treatment recommendation. Necrotic appearance, danger signals and adaptive antitumour immunity are separate questions.

Ferroptosis involves iron-dependent membrane-lipid peroxidation causing death. Erastin experiments implicated cystine uptake through system xc-, connecting cysteine and glutathione supply to antioxidant defence. Vulnerable polyunsaturated lipid chains, iron availability and cellular conditions matter; general reactive-oxygen fluorescence does not establish this mechanism.

GPX4 uses glutathione to reduce lipid hydroperoxides to lipid alcohols. FSP1 provides a parallel coenzyme-Q radical-trapping defence; it does not replace every GPX4 function or describe the whole protection network. Protein abundance alone does not measure protective activity or predict compound sensitivity.

Assigning ferroptosis needs convergent measurements of death, lipid damage preceding death, iron dependence and appropriately controlled rescue. Independent genetic and chemical perturbations strengthen attribution; rescue alone is not complete proof. Probe chemistry, concentration, nutrients, cell density and observation time can alter results. A lipid-probe ratio and death fraction are different outputs, with no universal diagnostic staining threshold. Live death and rescue tests consume viable model material. Specify lipid-probe oxidation ratios and independently measured death percentages over a stated interval; a marker snapshot does not reconstruct the full causal sequence.

A culture with abundant GPX4, a general oxidation signal and no death has not demonstrated ferroptosis. Cell-line and xenograft vulnerabilities do not establish tolerable exposure, selective cancer killing or benefit in patients. Alternative defences can confer resistance, so a strong antioxidant programme is not automatically a treatment vulnerability.

Hangauer 2017 investigated reversible drug-tolerant persister states across specified cancer-cell and drug models. Surviving the original treatment could coexist with increased GPX4 dependence; this was not necessarily permanent genetic resistance. The breast model BT474 is HER2-positive, not a triple-negative model. In the mouse relapse experiment, A375 melanoma cells had genetic GPX4 loss, with ferrostatin protection withdrawn while dabrafenib and trametinib continued. Prevented relapse in that setting was not systemic treatment with a GPX4 inhibitor: the authors noted poor systemic pharmacokinetics of RSL3 and ML210. These experiments do not establish a tolerable human window or universal persister vulnerability.

A fictional GPX4 experiment combines lipid oxidation before death, rescue by an iron chelator and a lipid-radical trap, and a corresponding phenotype after an independent genetic perturbation. These observations converge on an iron-dependent lipid-damage explanation; none alone proves it. Include vehicle, rescue-only and an unrelated death condition because rescue compounds can affect other processes. Survival of an otherwise matched FSP1-high comparison is compatible with a parallel defence; directly testing that defence is needed before assigning compensation to it. Energy production, a general oxidation dye and an antioxidant transcript are different measurements and cannot substitute for this causal sequence.
records.analogy: Ferroptosis is rust. Iron plus oxygen eats through the cell's membranes unless an antioxidant crew (GPX4) keeps repainting them. Cells that changed shape to dodge chemotherapy have thinner paint.

records.name: Functional (ex vivo) drug testing
records.tldr: Functional drug testing measures a defined response to medicines in collected living material under laboratory conditions.
records.summary: Functional drug testing exposes a defined living preparation to medicines and measures a specified response. Preparations may use dissociated cells, expanded organoids or short-term tissue cultures. Feasibility, outcome agreement and benefit from using a result to choose care are separate questions and must be tied to the actual assay version, cancer, treatment and setting.

notes: Specimen and assay card. Record donor/site/time, living preparation, transport and processing, initial composition, culture history, assay version, concentrations, exposure duration, replicates and control range. Fixed tissue cannot supply living cells; whether previously frozen material can supply the required viable preparation must be demonstrated for that protocol. Input suitability and recovery must be demonstrated for the method. Testing and endpoint processing use finite material. Output needs units, denominator, normalisation and uncertainty; acceptance criteria must be defined for the actual method. Name whether the preparation is dissociated cells, a fresh fragment or an expanded organoid. Mixed samples include normal neighbours, and expansion can change the represented populations.

Handling evidence is method-specific. Ladan and colleagues collected breast tissue in their specified medium, cut 300 micrometre slices and assessed morphology, proliferation and apoptosis after three-day exposure. This is not a general transport or storage protocol for all screens. Growth-rate methods show why baseline counts and control division affect interpretation. Retain failures and exclusions; failed preparation is not clinical resistance. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10542784/ ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4887336/ Medium, drug access and exposure duration can change the result. Mechanism-relevant controls test whether the claimed interaction can occur; absent required cells or unrealistic exposures can make an experiment uninformative even when a numerical response is available. A laboratory concentration is not a safe human dose.

Fictional example. A well has half the metabolic signal but the same identified viable tumour-cell endpoint count as control. This establishes a changed proxy, not half the cells killed; endpoint equality also does not reconstruct every division and death. Separate death, target engagement, safe human dosing and clinical benefit remain questions. This is an arithmetic and interpretation exercise, not observed patient data. Possible readouts include cell number, metabolism, mass, growth and death. Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is a cellular energy molecule measured by some luminescence assays. Promega's primary assay guidance states that cellular ATP content varies with cell type and physiology and can alter the relation between cell number and light output. A lower ATP signal can therefore reflect fewer cells or a per-cell change, rather than a counted death fraction. Source: https://www.promega.com/-/media/files/resources/protocols/technical-bulletins/0/celltiter-glo-luminescent-cell-viability-assay-protocol.pdf

Restivo and colleagues generated organoids from matched fresh and slow-frozen colorectal tumour tissue from two patients with stage IV disease. Their specified slow-freezing protocol used a cryoprotectant to preserve living material, and the frozen-derived cultures took longer to form than the fresh-derived cultures. This is evidence of recovery under that protocol, not equivalence of all fresh, snap-frozen and viable-cryopreserved samples or a guaranteed turnaround. The handling history, recovery, malignant identity and assay quality need checking for the intended experiment. Preserved molecular material alone does not establish a recoverable living model. records.name: Germline vs somatic mutations
records.tldr: A DNA change can be inherited, newly constitutional or acquired in a cell lineage. A change found in a tumor is not automatically tumor-specific.
records.summary: Inherited germline variants came through an egg or sperm and are generally present across many tissues. A de novo constitutional variant need not have been inherited from a parent. Changes arising after fertilization can create mosaic distributions. Somatic variants occur in body-cell lineages, including normal tissues as well as cancers. Origin, distribution, harmfulness and transmissibility are separate questions; neither a variant class nor a large read fraction settles them.

records.name: Glutamine addiction
records.tldr: Glutamine supports several cellular processes. A particular cell’s dependence on its metabolism must be tested under defined conditions.
records.summary: Glutamine enters via SLC1A5 (ASCT2) and SLC38A2; glutaminase (GLS, MYC-induced via miR-23 suppression; GLS2 is p53-induced) converts it to glutamate, which GLUD1 or transaminases (GOT1/2, GPT2) convert to α-ketoglutarate for TCA anaplerosis, supporting oxidative phosphorylation and, under hypoxia or IDH mutation, reductive carboxylation to citrate for lipids. Glutamine's amide nitrogen feeds purine and pyrimidine synthesis (CAD, PPAT) and hexosamines; glutamate makes glutathione (with cysteine via SLC7A11) and aspartate (KRAS-mutant pancreatic cancer routes glutamine through GOT1 to maintain NADPH). mTORC1 senses glutamine-derived α-KG. Tumour uptake depletes glutamine in the microenvironment, impairing T-cell effector function. Drugs: the glutaminase inhibitor telaglenastat (CB-839) failed in RCC (CANTATA) and was tested in the KEAP1/NRF2-selected NSCLC KEAPSAKE combination trial, whose registry records termination for lack of clinical benefit; the broad glutamine antagonist prodrug DRP-104 (sirpiglenastat) and ASCT2 inhibitors are in early trials; asparaginase (which also depletes glutamine) is standard in ALL. Glutamine PET tracers (18F-FGln) image glioma where FDG fails.

records.name: Double-strand break repair: HR versus end joining
records.tldr: Cells can repair breaks through both DNA strands using a matching template or several end-joining routes. The available template, cell state and broken ends affect which route can operate.
records.summary:
Double-strand breaks can be repaired through matching-template homologous recombination or several end-joining routes. Homologous repair often uses the sister chromatid after DNA copying. The substrate, available template and cell-cycle state affect which route can operate.

Preparing a double-strand break for homologous repair includes DNA end resection in the 5′ to 3′ direction, leaving protruding 3′ single-stranded ends. RAD51 helps a prepared strand find and pair with a complementary strand in matching duplex DNA, displacing the other template strand into a D-loop. DNA synthesis can then extend the invading end using the template. Synthesis-dependent strand annealing can finish as a noncrossover repair: the extended strand leaves the template and pairs with the other broken end. Other homologous-repair routes can have crossover outcomes, so using an intact template does not mean every repair leaves donor and recipient arrangements unchanged. Purified bacterial RecA structures reveal strand-pairing intermediates; they are not direct measurements of human RAD51 repair in a tumour.

Classical nonhomologous end joining reconnects ends without requiring a long matching template and can preserve compatible ends. Microhomology-associated joining uses short matching sequences after end processing. Theta-mediated end joining names a POLQ-mediated mechanism; finding short matches alone does not identify that enzyme. These routes overlap in outcomes without becoming interchangeable definitions.

Ku binds broken ends, and ligase IV with supporting factors can help align and seal them; difficult ends can require processing. Resection exposes single-stranded regions for alternative joining, where short matches can align and intervening sequence can be lost. Purified-factor experiments, defined chromosome-break reporters and controlled cellular studies test particular substrates and factor dependencies, not a universal menu for every break.

A fictional top-strand sequence CA-GAC-TT|AA-GAC-GT has 14 base pairs before joining. A selected short-match product CA-GAC-GT retains seven, losing the four-base TTAA interval and one three-base GAC repeat. For a selected alignment of GAC with its complementary CTG sequence, trimming the unmatched TT flaps leaves seven paired positions and two backbone nicks to seal, without a gap to fill. Other substrates can require synthesis; this arithmetic and schematic geometry are not measured repair frequencies.

Sequence a repaired junction and measure a defined repair reporter, then perturb the proposed factor with specificity controls and, where feasible, rescue. Repair fraction, junction distribution and cell survival are distinct outputs. A deletion with microhomology is compatible with a joining route, but does not demonstrate POLQ dependence, selective killing or benefit from a POLQ inhibitor in a patient. Viable-cell and purified-component studies have model-specific input and material costs.

records.name: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD)
records.tldr: Homologous recombination deficiency means that a template-guided DNA repair process is impaired. A gene finding, a genomic scar and current repair function provide different evidence.
records.summary:
A repair-gene finding suggests a possible cause, a genomic scar records accumulated consequences, and a functional assay tests present behavior. A variant is not automatically damaging, loss of one copy is not automatically loss of both, and repair can recover while historical scars persist. None of these observations alone is the probability of clinical benefit.

Homologous recombination uses sufficiently matching DNA, often the sister chromatid after copying, to repair certain breaks. BRCA1 helps coordinate repair; BRCA2 helps RAD51 assemble on prepared single-stranded DNA to search and pair with a template. Template availability and cell-cycle state matter. In a fictional model with both functional BRCA2 copies lost, template-guided repair is impaired and alternative joining can leave deletions and rearrangements, but the sequence of a scar does not uniquely identify the cause or every protein that acted.

A low RAD51-focus count is interpretable only with adequate tumor cells, an appropriate cycling population and evidence that the cells experienced damage. Cruz 2018 assessed RAD51 with geminin as an S/G2 marker and gamma-H2AX as a damage marker in patient-derived models and retrospective tumor specimens. Fixed tissue can support this functional-surrogate approach; functional does not always mean live drug culture. An inadequate sample is uninformative, and a research assay needs analytical and clinical validation for its intended use.

Telli tested scar-score associations with response to platinum-containing chemotherapy before surgery in triple-negative breast cancer; that result does not establish a universal PARP-inhibitor cutoff. Farmer demonstrated sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-deficient cell models, a separate evidence setting. The U.S. olaparib early-breast-cancer label specifies deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA findings, HER2-negative high-risk disease, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy and companion-diagnostic selection. A tumor-only result or high scar score does not replace those criteria.

A coherent collection of markers is not a vote that turns all five claims into one label.

Two fictional models can share compatible historical scars yet have different current behaviour. Adequate assays in A support impaired repair, target engagement is demonstrated, and survival falls after the tested exposure. B instead shows partial repair restoration and little survival change despite engagement. The first pattern supports a repair-related sensitivity hypothesis in A; the scar overstates B's current vulnerability. Restoring repair in A could test causality. Conversely, few RAD51 foci with almost no cycling cells can be uninformative even when a culture survives a PARP exposure: record the compatible history, inadequate functional result and observed survival separately. None of these model results determines a treatment indication.

records.name: HRD genomic scar scores (GIS, LOH, HRDetect)
records.tldr: These scores measure selected patterns of accumulated chromosome change. The assay and cutoff matter; a high score alone does not establish current repair failure or treatment eligibility.
records.summary:
Genomic scars are historical patterns in sampled tumor DNA. They can remain after a surviving population restores homologous repair, so a scar result is not a direct measurement of current function or a guarantee of drug benefit. DNA extraction consumes material; purity, ploidy estimation, segmentation, specimen quality and algorithm version affect the reported result. Counts are not percentages of cells whose repair has failed.

Loss of heterozygosity means losing one parental version, with or without a reduction in total copy number. Abkevich 2012 counted LOH regions longer than 15 megabases but shorter than a whole chromosome in epithelial ovarian cancer analyses. Birkbak counted imbalanced regions reaching a telomere without crossing the centromere. Popova studied transitions between adjacent regions at least 10 megabases long in basal-like breast carcinoma. The original LST method estimated counts separately within each chromosome arm, excluding centromeric breaks, after filtering and smoothing variations smaller than 3 megabases. Segment filters and clinical score cutoffs are different rules.

A composite score can sum different scar features. Telli 2016 used the unweighted sum of LOH, telomeric allelic imbalance and large-scale transitions, with a predefined high-score boundary reported as 42 in the abstract, or a deleterious BRCA1/2 finding, in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials. The training population used to choose a boundary, the treated population used to test response, the assay scale and the intended use are different facts. A number on another assay cannot be read against this threshold without validation; a response association is not an interchangeable treatment-selection rule.

In a fictional, already filtered within-arm profile, a 12-megabase segment next to an 8-megabase segment fails the requirement that both neighbors be at least 10 megabases. A 12-megabase segment next to a 14-megabase segment meets that size component. This tests counting, not a 10-megabase deletion rule, present repair function or a clinical response cutoff. The original algorithm filters and validation population still apply.

notes: A composite score compresses selected features of a tumour's chromosome history. Like a summary of past events, it leaves details out; like numbers on differently calibrated scales, the same numerical value need not have the same meaning in two laboratories. The composite count is not a percentage of repair-deficient cells. Copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity can replace two parental versions with copies of one version without reducing the total copy number, so loss of heterozygosity is not always loss of a physical chromosome copy.

Telli 2016 selected the boundary of 42 using an independent training set of 497 breast and 561 ovarian cancers, including 78 breast and 190 ovarian cancers classified as lacking a functional BRCA1 or BRCA2 copy. That classification used a deleterious variant with loss of the other copy, two deleterious changes in one gene, or BRCA1 promoter methylation with loss of the other copy. The boundary was the fifth percentile among these BRCA-deficient cancers, aiming to capture about 95 per cent, rather than an optimised divider of drug responders. Some deficient cancers therefore fall below it. The study's abstract and discussion use at least 42, whereas its Methods prints greater than 42; a result at the boundary needs the actual validated assay rule, not an improvised inequality.

Telli tested the unweighted LOH plus TAI plus LST score in three platinum-containing neoadjuvant triple-negative breast cancer trials, using a high score or a deleterious or suspected-deleterious tumour BRCA1/2 alteration. A variant of uncertain significance did not count as a mutated BRCA result. The odds ratios for minimal residual disease, residual cancer burden class 0 or I, were 4.96 in PrECOG's platinum, gemcitabine and iniparib cohort and 10.18 in the pooled two cisplatin cohorts. These associations are not three randomised demonstrations of extra platinum benefit. PRIMA later defined HRD positivity by a tumour BRCA mutation or a MyChoice genomic instability score of at least 42. That trial definition and current prescribing conditions are separate facts.

ARIEL2 Part 1 used a prespecified 14 per cent genomic-LOH cutoff in relapsed, platinum-sensitive high-grade ovarian cancer. Of 206 enrolled patients, 204 received rucaparib and 192 could be classified: 40 BRCA-mutated, 82 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-high and 70 BRCA-wild-type/LOH-low. Twelve BRCA-wild-type tumours lacked enough neoplastic nuclei for the LOH classification. This percentage of genome is a different quantity from the composite sum, and a single-arm rucaparib study cannot by itself separate prognostic association from differential treatment benefit. HRDetect is different again: its weighted sequence-signature logistic model outputs a probability of BRCA-deficient genomic history. Its 2017 sensitivity and AUC describe that classification task, not an individual's chance of benefiting from a medicine.

In the GeparSixto analysis, HRD was measurable in 193 of 315 triple-negative breast cancers. Pathological complete response rose from 33.9 to 63.5 per cent with added carboplatin in the HR-deficient group and from 20.0 to 29.6 per cent in the other group. The treatment-by-HRD interaction had P = 0.327. This does not establish that the treatment effects differ by HRD status, nor does a non-significant interaction prove they are identical. In TNT, 376 people with advanced triple-negative disease or a germline BRCA-associated breast cancer received carboplatin or docetaxel. Germline-BRCA carriers had response rates of 68 versus 33 per cent, with interaction P = 0.01; a high Myriad HRD score did not select extra carboplatin benefit. Association with response and evidence for choosing between treatments are different questions.

PAOLA-1 randomised 806 people with advanced ovarian cancer responding to first-line platinum-taxane chemotherapy plus bevacizumab. Both maintenance groups received bevacizumab; the added treatment was olaparib or placebo. The 2019 HRD-positive progression-free-survival hazard ratio was 0.33, with a 95 per cent interval of 0.25 to 0.45. The olaparib label's planned exploratory HRD-negative analysis gives 1.00, with an interval of 0.75 to 1.34. That interval is compatible with a range of effects and does not prove exactly zero benefit. It also cannot be transferred to an unrelated assay, breast cancer, a different drug or olaparib without bevacizumab.

PRIMA's 2019 analysis randomised 733 people after response to first-line platinum for advanced ovarian cancer. Among 373 with HR-deficient tumours, median progression-free survival was 21.9 versus 10.4 months with niraparib versus placebo, hazard ratio 0.43 with a 95 per cent interval of 0.31 to 0.59. In the overall population it was 13.8 versus 8.2 months, hazard ratio 0.62 with an interval of 0.50 to 0.76. These are historical progression-free-survival results, not an updated overall-survival estimate. The U.S. niraparib label effective July 2026 restricts first-line maintenance to HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to platinum, selected with an authorised companion test.

The U.S. olaparib label effective July 2025 permits olaparib plus bevacizumab maintenance for adults with HRD-positive advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer in complete or partial response to first-line platinum; the specified HRD definition includes a deleterious or suspected-deleterious BRCA alteration and/or genomic instability, with an approved companion test. Its early-breast indication instead requires a deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA alteration, HER2-negative high-risk disease and prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, with the approved test. A tumour-only BRCA finding or an arbitrary high scar number does not substitute for these conditions.

The specimen and analysis are part of the result. Telli used tumour DNA, a genome-wide SNP panel, allele-imbalance profiles and prespecified counting rules; if the score failed and BRCA testing was negative or failed, HRD status was undetermined. A failed result is not a low score. Reports should identify the assay version, usable tumour content, DNA input/quality, copy-number and allele-balance method, segmentation, and purity/ploidy assumptions. HRDetect was explored in a small biopsy series and one formalin-fixed specimen with substantial sequencing artefact; those demonstrations do not certify every degraded specimen. RAD51 foci ask a different, conditional question about present repair. A BRCA reversion or 53BP1 loss is not itself a measured new scar score or proof of restored function.

In a fictional report, laboratory X gives a score of 48 and a paper uses laboratory Y's cutoff of 42 in early triple-negative breast cancer. The numerical comparison 48 > 42 does not establish HRD positivity on X's assay: its scale, quality requirements and validated boundary are needed. Even on the correct scale, association with response to one regimen does not establish extra carboplatin benefit over a comparator. GeparSixto's interaction analysis and TNT's high-score result illustrate that distinction; neither permits a blanket claim that a high-score tumour never benefits from carboplatin.

records.name: KEAP1-NRF2 antioxidant pathway
records.tldr: KEAP1-NRF2 regulates cellular stress defences. Protection, metabolic dependence and treatment response need separate tests in the relevant cancer and conditions.
records.summary:
KEAP1 helps a CUL3-containing ubiquitin-ligase system regulate NRF2 turnover. Loss of relevant KEAP1 function can stabilise NRF2 and increase antioxidant, detoxification and drug-export programmes. A gene alteration or high RNA signal alone does not establish its functional direction, the affected cells or a treatment response.

Singh 2006 identified KEAP1 mutations in ten of 54 non-small-cell lung cancer samples, including primary tumours and pleural fluid. Among six mutation-bearing primary tumours assessed for the remaining locus, five had loss of heterozygosity. The cell experiments supported increased NRF2-related activity and drug-resistance mechanisms in those systems, rather than resistance to every therapy.

Romero 2017 used gene editing and metabolic experiments in KRAS-driven lung cancer models: Keap1 loss promoted tumour growth and created a glutaminolysis vulnerability in the tested systems. A protective programme can therefore coexist with a dependence on a different supply route. The randomised phase 2 KEAPSAKE registry records 40 actual participants and termination for lack of clinical benefit from the telaglenastat combination strategy. A preclinical dependence is not an approved treatment or a universal predictor of benefit.

Singh's initial series contained 40 primary lung cancers and 16 pleural-fluid samples; excluding two small-cell pleural-fluid samples gives the 54 NSCLC denominator. Ten mutation-bearing samples round to 19 per cent, not a universal lung-cancer prevalence. Five of six tested mutation-bearing primary tumours had locus loss; do not assign biallelic loss to all ten samples. Romero separately described KEAP1 alterations in about 20 per cent of KRAS-mutant lung adenocarcinomas. These populations and denominators differ. KEAP1-mutant-versus-normal-cell viability comparisons are not matched isogenic proof that one alteration caused every chemotherapy response.

Protection and dependence are experiment-specific directions. If removing a verified defence makes a defined stress more lethal, that supports protection under that stress. If removing the defence or a supply route reduces survival relative to an appropriate matched comparison, that supports a conditional dependence; it need not mean every unstressed cell dies. In a fictional culture, high antioxidant RNA plus probe-associated death establishes neither NRF2-driven killing nor ferroptosis. Test the alteration's effect on NRF2 turnover or nuclear localisation and output, then use independent perturbation and restoration to examine the survival mechanism. CUL3 works with other adaptors, and a compound suppressing protein production broadly does not isolate NRF2. A genetic intervention also needs controls, rather than being automatically specific.

The record last updated in September 2022 reports actual enrollment 40, status terminated and the stated reason lack of clinical benefit. This is registry status, not a peer-reviewed effect estimate or proof that every glutaminase strategy fails. Model activity, eligibility, acceptable exposure and clinical benefit remain different questions.
records.analogy: A large fire service could reflect frequent fires, effective protection or dependence on a particular fuel supply. Counting equipment alone cannot distinguish those explanations; the corresponding cellular questions require activity, perturbation and survival measurements.

records.name: Kinase
records.tldr: A kinase transfers a phosphate group to a substrate. The effect depends on which molecule and site are modified.
records.summary: Many protein kinases transfer phosphate from ATP to selected substrate residues, commonly serine, threonine or tyrosine, leaving ADP. Phosphatases remove phosphate through a different reaction, rather than simply making ATP by reversing kinase activity. Kinases can also modify lipids, as PI3K does. Protein amount is distinct from catalytic activity, and not every relay protein is a kinase. In the defined EGFR asymmetric-dimer mechanism, activation-loop phosphorylation was not required for activation.

records.name: Lipid synthesis, uptake & cholesterol
records.tldr: Cells can make, import, store and reuse lipids. The route they use and their dependence on it vary with the cell and conditions.
records.summary: Lipid metabolism includes synthesis, uptake, storage, membrane remodelling and oxidation. Cholesterol regulation and fatty-acid regulation overlap but are not interchangeable. Identify the SREBP member, cellular compartment and measured output rather than treating a transcript, precursor, nuclear fragment, sterol amount and synthesis rate as the same observation. SCAP-SREBP transport responds to endoplasmic reticulum cholesterol in the cited cell experiments. The mevalonate pathway supplies sterols and nonsterol products, including substrates for protein prenylation. Rescue by mevalonate therefore cannot uniquely identify cholesterol as the limiting product. Transcript abundance, lipid abundance, labelled production and a controlled survival-dependence experiment answer different questions. Results from a particular cell model or mouse experiment do not establish a universal tumour vulnerability or a preferred diet or treatment.
