notes: SCAP and local endoplasmic-reticulum sterol conditions regulate transport of membrane-bound SREBP to the Golgi. Processing releases a fragment that enters the nucleus and regulates lipid synthesis and uptake. Sufficient local sterol supply can retain the complex in the ER; total cellular cholesterol and SREBP RNA do not measure this processing.

In the fictional supply experiment, nuclear SREBP-2 and uptake messages respond to lipid-poor medium; external lipid supply can reduce the response and compensate for synthesis perturbation. Record medium composition, density, timing and viability before assigning dependence. A supply-sensitive state does not establish the response of a person's tumour. Assess precursor and nuclear regulator, responsive transcripts, cellular sterols and uptake separately from labelled synthesis rates. Use controlled supplementation to test the proposed bottleneck; total amount does not specify production or local sensing.

In transgenic mice expressing a truncated SREBP-2 construct, Horton and colleagues observed preferential activation of cholesterol synthesis over fatty-acid synthesis in liver and adipose tissue, contrasting it with earlier SREBP-1a results. They separately measured transcripts and synthesis using labelled water. These are relative effects in a named experimental system, not exclusive duties of each family member or proof that a transcript measurement equals flux. Precursor location and nuclear processing require their own measurements.

Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase upstream in the mevalonate pathway, which supplies cholesterol and nonsterol products. In Freed-Pastor and colleagues' breast-cancer 3D cultures, geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate partially rescued an invasive phenotype after mutant-p53 depletion or simvastatin treatment. This illustrates why mevalonate rescue alone cannot uniquely attribute an effect to cholesterol. It does not identify every relevant metabolite, establish a universal cancer dependency or show that a statin perturbation reproduces every change in SCAP-SREBP regulation.

HMG-CoA reductase makes mevalonate and is inhibited by statins. The downstream pathway branches: farnesyl pyrophosphate, FPP, feeds sterol synthesis through squalene and GGPP production as well as supplying protein prenylation; geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate, GGPP, supplies another prenylation route. Farnesyl and geranylgeranyl lipid modifications help position specified RAS- and RHO-family proteins, respectively. Cholesterol is a membrane component and a precursor of steroid hormones. Cholesterol amount, sterol synthesis and the whole mevalonate pathway are therefore different measurements. SCAP-SREBP sterol sensing regulates synthesis and uptake, but its activity, pathway transcripts, metabolite supply and dependence must each be established in the tested cells and medium.

Freed-Pastor 2012 studied mutant-p53 breast cancer cells in three-dimensional culture, with different outcomes in two triple-negative lines. Depleting mutant p53 reduced invasive behaviour in MDA-MB-231 but did not make it form ordered hollow acini; MDA-MB-468 could acquire a more ordered, hollow architecture. Statins reduced invasion in the former and caused growth inhibition with extensive death in the latter, rather than exactly reproducing every p53-depletion phenotype. Mutant-p53 depletion reduced mevalonate-pathway expression, and mevalonate add-back opposed several statin effects. This supports a pathway contribution in the studied systems without isolating cholesterol. The whole paper also examined growth, death and xenograft growth; it was not solely an architecture experiment, and none of these results established patient treatment benefit.

The branch experiments further narrowed an invasive-morphology question in MDA-MB-231. Blocking the geranylgeranylation branch had a larger effect than the tested sterol-branch block, and GGPP partly restored invasive growth after mutant-p53 depletion or statin treatment. That is not evidence that GGPP rescues inhibition of the transferase itself, nor that every effect in both cell lines was entirely explained by one metabolite. The authors allowed contributions from other products. In a fictional supply comparison, synthesis falls under an inhibitor in both lipid-poor and lipid-rich medium, but growth slows mainly in the former while import is stipulated to compensate in the latter. Equal engagement with different growth outcomes is compatible with environmental supply; it is not a measurement of supply or dependence in a person's tumour.
records.analogy: A factory that must build its own walls. Normal adult tissue buys wall panels from a supplier (dietary fat); cancer reopens its own panel plant (FASN) and, when it lands in a fat depot, simply strips panels off the buildings next door.

records.name: Metastasis
records.tldr: Metastasis is the establishment of cancer at a distant site. Finding cells in transit or in another tissue does not by itself demonstrate sustained distant growth.
records.summary: Cancer cells may leave a primary site, travel through blood or lymph, reach another tissue and establish a growing lesion. Many steps can fail. Regional lymph-node involvement differs from distant metastasis, and the distant deposit retains the identity of the primary cancer. Clinical interpretation depends on the represented sites and disease context.

A circulating tumour cell is found in blood; a disseminated tumour cell has reached tissue away from the primary. Neither observation alone establishes an enlarging distant lesion, and regional lymph-node involvement differs from distant metastasis.

A breast-cancer deposit in lung retains breast primary identity, while a separate lung primary is another possibility requiring tissue and clinical interpretation. Imaging and pathology identify represented sites; research tracking and environmental perturbations address different biological questions. Negative findings retain the sensitivity and sampling limits of the method. Arrival, survival, sustained growth and the mechanism maintaining or ending restraint need separate evidence.

records.name: Necrosis
records.tldr: Necrosis describes cell and tissue breakdown with loss of membrane integrity. The appearance alone does not identify its cause.
records.summary: Necrotic appearance can follow overwhelming injury or regulated death mechanisms. A late membrane-integrity measurement cannot reconstruct the preceding death sequence. Histology describes the sampled region; necrosis there does not establish the absence of viable tumour elsewhere, treatment success or a particular molecular pathway. Distinguish tissue appearance from a mechanism established by controlled perturbation and complementary readouts. Inflammation and antigen-specific adaptive immune protection are separate outcomes.

Histology describes the sampled region; viable tumour may remain elsewhere. A membrane-compromised fraction, qualitative tissue necrosis and method-defined necrotic area answer different questions. Handling, delayed fixation and late sampling affect interpretation, and no universal necrosis percentage identifies a death mechanism or proves treatment success. Preparing and staining a section consumes tissue, while live-cell dye assays use tested aliquots and report a defined membrane-compromised fraction. Clinical morphology and experimental pathway perturbation have different validation contexts.

HMGB1-deficient necrotic cells produced less inflammation in defined experiments. That result concerns danger signalling, rather than automatic adaptive immune memory. Dye entry after an intervention cannot establish necroptosis, vaccine activity or clinical benefit without the separate causal and host tests.

records.name: Neoadjuvant / adjuvant / perioperative
records.tldr: Neoadjuvant treatment comes before the main treatment, usually surgery; adjuvant treatment follows it to lower recurrence risk. These words describe roles in a plan, while its goal and actual delivery need separate assessment.
records.summary:
Neoadjuvant treatment precedes the main treatment, usually surgery; adjuvant treatment follows the main treatment to reduce recurrence risk. Perioperative treatment spans the period around an operation. Neoadjuvant therapy can aim to reduce disease before an operation and provides response information from treated tissue. Adjuvant therapy aims to reduce risk from disease that may remain. A pathological response and a later clinical outcome are different endpoints.

Timing comparisons need the actual population, intervention and comparator. Liu’s two mouse breast-cancer models supported testing preoperative immunotherapy, not a universal human timing rule or proof that retained tumour antigen explains every clinical result. KEYNOTE-522 assigned a complete before-and-after pembrolizumab regimen against its comparator; that design does not independently randomize the two phases and cannot isolate each phase’s contribution.

Neoadjuvant treatment can reduce a tumour before an operation and leave treated tissue for response assessment. Subsequent breast and nodal pathology, radiation indications and further systemic options answer separate questions. Residual disease does not automatically choose one added medicine: prior treatment, biomarker eligibility, the population actually studied and uncertainty about sequencing or combination remain relevant. A pathological response is not a survival estimate or proof that a treatment component can be omitted.

Either, both or neither surrounding phase may appear in a plan. Chemotherapy, radiation, endocrine and other treatments can have preoperative or postoperative roles in appropriate settings. Systemic therapy travels through the bloodstream; neither timing word means chemotherapy alone. An adjuvant plan can aim to reduce risk even when there is no measurable tumour, and it does not guarantee that recurrence is impossible.

A drug that happens before a procedure is not automatically neoadjuvant. In a fictional curative-intent plan, systemic treatment precedes definitive breast surgery and additional treatment afterwards aims to reduce recurrence risk. In a different advanced-disease plan, a later procedure relieves a symptom. Both calendars say drug then procedure, but the documented main-treatment role and goal distinguish them.

Preoperative treatment can provide examination and imaging observations and treated surgical tissue for assessing response. CREATE-X selected residual invasive disease after preoperative chemotherapy; OlympiA included eligible high-risk germline BRCA1/2-associated disease after either neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, using different entry rules. These studies show why treatment history and response can affect the next question. They do not make a favourable response a validated surgery-omission rule or prove that every postoperative add-on helps.

Keep specimen collection, treatment administration and report issue as three dates. A biopsy collected before treatment remains a pretreatment sample even if its report arrives after surgery. Likewise, a planned treatment phase is not proof of administration: holds, substitutions and cancelled visits belong in the delivered record. Timing of a report cannot manufacture a post-treatment observation.

Treatment timing does not itself establish curative or palliative anticancer intent. Palliative care addresses symptoms, distress and quality of life and can accompany curative care. Thus a fictional postoperative risk-reduction plan is adjuvant even without visible tumour, and a supportive-care visit does not turn it into palliative anticancer treatment. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) is one neoadjuvant class; a vaccine adjuvant instead means an ingredient that enhances an immune response.

records.name: Notch signalling
records.tldr: Notch receptors can relay signals between contacting cells. The effect depends on the receptor, ligand, alteration and tissue; receiving a signal does not by itself prove growth dependence.
records.summary:
A ligand-bearing sender, receptor amount, received signal and growth dependence are separate observations. Locate malignant, vessel and other neighboring cells before assigning a Notch mechanism. Ligand on a vessel is not evidence that the tumor received the signal, and total receptor is different from a released nuclear intracellular domain.

Common contact-dependent Notch signaling begins when Delta-like or Jagged ligand on one cell engages a receptor on a neighbor. Ligand-regulated extracellular cleavage permits subsequent gamma-secretase-mediated membrane cleavage; the released Notch intracellular domain, NICD, can enter the nucleus and work with transcriptional partners. This route differs from an RTK phosphorylation relay and omits receptor maturation and sender mechanics.

Weng found activating NOTCH1 changes in extracellular heterodimerization or PEST regions in more than half of the studied T-ALLs. Agrawal identified predicted inactivating alterations in head-and-neck squamous tumors, suggesting a tumor-suppressor role there. An uncharacterized allele inherits neither direction from the pathway name; tissue, cell identity and alteration effect matter.

A fictional T-ALL culture with high nuclear NICD without a ligand-bearing neighbor, and lower NICD after gamma-secretase blockade, supports a ligand-independent activation hypothesis. A contact-blocking experiment that lowers NICD without changing growth instead supports reduced received signaling without demonstrating a growth requirement. Control general toxicity, contact conditions, independent pathway perturbations and compensation. Gamma-secretase also processes other proteins; responsive HES/HEY RNA and nuclear staining need validated assays and are not universal eligibility cutoffs.

A NOTCH2 fusion encoded an active intracellular product that bypassed the cleavage step and its model resisted that inhibitor. Position alone was not sufficient: a NOTCH1-rearranged line with low active-NOTCH1 signal also resisted. Both the actual active product and model conditions matter. The experiment does not make all activated Notch equivalent, validate a universal staining cutoff or establish a clinical selection rule.

records.name: AMPK energy sensing
records.tldr: AMPK helps cells adjust their work to their energy supply. Slower growth and better survival can occur together.
records.summary: AMP-activated protein kinase responds to cellular energy state. Structural and biochemical experiments showed that ADP binding protects activating phosphorylation without the direct allosteric activation supplied by AMP. In cancer-model experiments during energy stress, AMPK supported NADPH maintenance through changes in fatty-acid metabolism and prolonged survival. Thus activation cannot be read as a universal cancer-killing signal. Preserve the model, energy conditions, timing, perturbation controls and separate measurements of growth and death. A phosphorylation signal does not establish selective drug action or patient benefit.

notes: AMP-activated protein kinase is a catalytic and regulatory complex responding to energy state. AMP and ADP can protect activating phosphorylation, but AMP also supplies direct allosteric activation that ADP does not. ATP, ADP and AMP quantities and ratios are different from a phosphoprotein readout.

LKB1 and a calcium-sensitive CaMKK2 route can activate AMPK in suitable systems. AMPK can phosphorylate raptor and restrain mTORC1, connecting energy supply to costly growth-related work. An AMPK phosphosite does not uniquely identify glucose deprivation or every nutrient signal.

During energy stress in model experiments, AMPK preserved reducing power through altered fatty-acid metabolism and supported survival. Increased AMPK and raptor phosphorylation, slower growth and greater survival than an AMPK-deficient comparison are compatible observations. This is not a universal benefit from activating or inhibiting AMPK.

Keep collection timing, preservation, total protein, antibody specificity and matched perturbations with energy-state and phosphosite measurements. Mixed tissue can combine malignant and nonmalignant responses. Slower growth is not death, an altered gene needs direction-of-function evidence, and a marker change does not make a multitarget drug a selective AMPK intervention. Report concentrations or ratios of energy carriers, normalised activating phosphorylation and defined downstream sites. Preserved tissue can support staining, while viable-model perturbations use material. No universal AMPK-high cutoff establishes vulnerability.

records.tldr: Off-label use means using an approved medicine outside its approved labeling. The evidence for that particular use and whether it will be paid for need separate assessment.

The supporting evidence can vary. A product never approved for any use is investigational rather than simply off label; clinical trials and expanded access have different arrangements. records.tldr: Olaparib was the first PARP inhibitor, and turned an inherited BRCA mutation from a risk factor into a drug target, including after surgery in breast cancer.

Prostate monotherapy covers germline or somatic HRR-gene-mutated mCRPC after enzalutamide or abiraterone; the abiraterone/prednisone combination is BRCA selected. The later report demonstrated an overall-survival benefit at its own planned analysis. Post-neoadjuvant capecitabine was not permitted in OlympiA, so it cannot compare olaparib with capecitabine in that setting. CREATE-X studied additional capecitabine after specified chemotherapy. records.name: Oxidative phosphorylation
records.tldr: Oxygen use and cellular energy production are related measurements. Researchers need controlled experiments to work out how much energy a cell produces through mitochondrial respiration.
records.summary: Extracellular flux methods estimate respiratory and glycolytic contributions to energy production under defined assumptions. A respiratory message, measured oxygen use, calculated energy output and dependence for survival are distinct claims. Normalisation, fuel, viable-cell input, collection time and the specified method version belong with a result. Electron transport, proton pumping, return through ATP synthase and uncoupling are distinct steps. The mitochondrial matrix and intermembrane space locate the two sides of the inner membrane; naming these compartments does not supply a universal conversion ratio.

notes: Respiration and ATP generation are related but different measurements. Mitochondrial and nonmitochondrial oxygen consumption, proton leak and ATP-linked respiration require controlled separation. Respiratory transcripts, normalised oxygen-consumption rates and survival dependence cannot substitute for one another; bulk tissue composition and compensatory fuel use also matter. Oxygen-consumption assays require viable cells or functional preparations rather than routine fixed sections and use or perturb the tested material. Report oxygen per time with justified viable-cell or protein normalisation. Equal baseline respiration and different responses to ATP-synthase inhibition do not by themselves identify which culture will die.

The fictional oxygen-rate example gives 60 minus 30 = 30 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 viable cells after ATP-synthase inhibition. This is an inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference, not picomoles of ATP, a death percentage or a corrected ATP-production calculation. Fuel, normalisation and assay controls remain attached.

In mitochondria, respiratory electron transfer and proton movement are distinct processes. Some respiratory complexes move protons from the matrix into the intermembrane space; return through ATP synthase can support ATP formation, while other return pathways dissipate the gradient without that synthesis step. These directions do not specify a fixed proton-to-ATP ratio. Protons return from the intermembrane space to the matrix through the membrane-embedded Fo part of ATP synthase. The matrix-facing F1 part uses the transferred energy to make ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. Protons provide the driving force; they are not converted into ATP. A parallel proton leak bypasses ATP synthase and dissipates the gradient. In Racker and Stoeckenius' reconstituted vesicles, a light-driven membrane system from Halobacterium supported ATP formation when mitochondrial ATPase was included. Their artificial vesicles pumped in the opposite direction to the intact source cells, so the experiment supports coupling without specifying a universal cellular orientation or ratio.

Extracellular acidification can include respiration-derived carbon dioxide as well as glycolytic acid production. Keep correction assumptions, normalisation and method version with any calculated ATP rate. The 2018 correction to Mookerjee and colleagues' 2017 method changes the ATP-linked oxygen-rate equation and reports use of a different hyperpolarization factor in some calculations; several numerical rates changed while the authors retained their qualitative conclusions. An inhibitor-sensitive oxygen-rate difference is therefore not itself an ATP rate, and an unversioned fixed conversion should not be inferred.

In a fictional paired-well example, culture A uses 180 picomoles of oxygen per minute with 30,000 viable cells and B uses 120 with 20,000. Both equal 60 per minute per 10,000 viable cells. After ATP-synthase blockade their corresponding normalised rates are 30 and 40, giving inhibitor-sensitive differences of 30 and 20 picomoles of oxygen per minute per 10,000 cells. Those are oxygen-rate differences, not ATP-production rates or proof of survival dependence. Cell number, fuel, oxygen, timing and the inhibitor controls matter. A corrected, specified conversion method needs additional assumptions; the 2018 Mookerjee correction changed calculations by up to 17 per cent. General oxidation, compartment-specific reactive chemistry and iron-dependent lipid death remain separate questions.

Echeverria 2019 treated three patient-derived triple-negative breast cancer xenograft models with doxorubicin and cyclophosphamide. Barcode structure was broadly maintained at the residual nadir; regrowth could select dominant barcodes, so this does not exclude all clonal selection. In PIM001-P, the RNA analysis highlighted oxidative phosphorylation and isolated residual cells had higher oxygen consumption and lower extracellular acidification than untreated cells. Those rate measurements were not obtained in every model. IACS-010759 delayed regrowth after chemotherapy in the three tested models, rather than eradicating the tumours. Regrown models could again respond to chemotherapy. Two serial human biopsy cases supported stability during initial AC but did not establish invariant clones through all subsequent treatment. Rate, state, perturbation response and clinical benefit remain distinct evidence.

Yap 2023 reported phase 1 IACS-010759 studies in 17 people with acute myeloid leukaemia and 23 with advanced solid tumours. Elevated blood lactate and neurotoxicity limited exposure needed for sustained complex-I inhibition; target inhibition was modest, antitumour activity limited, no recommended phase 2 dose was established and both studies were discontinued. These named safety and exposure results separate a model vulnerability from a usable treatment. A respiratory RNA signature plus a lower ATP-based signal still establishes neither increased oxygen-consumption rate nor counted cell death. Measure identified viable cells, normalised oxygen use, engagement and independent growth or death outcomes. Acidification can include respiratory carbon dioxide as well as glycolysis, and lactate production with oxygen can coexist with respiration.

records.name: PARP inhibitors
records.tldr: These medicines disrupt DNA repair processes. Some also retain repair proteins on DNA; a repair-gene finding alone does not establish that they will help.
records.summary: PARP inhibitors reduce PARP enzyme activity and can stabilise PARP complexes on damaged DNA. Catalytic output, DNA-associated occupancy, repair capacity and cell survival are different measurements. Experimental sensitivity depends on the current cellular repair state, and repair-restoring changes can contribute to resistance. Clinical eligibility depends on the particular medicine, cancer setting, previous treatment and required companion test; a shared mechanism is not a shared indication.

notes: PARP means poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase, a protein family involved in cellular signalling and repair. PARP1 is one representative. At damaged DNA it can build signals on proteins from chains of the chemical unit ADP-ribose, called poly(ADP-ribose), or PAR. Catalytic inhibition reduces this output. Some inhibitors can also stabilise DNA-associated PARP complexes, often called trapping. A repair-worker analogy separates a reduced call for help from a worker remaining in a doorway; proteins and medicines have no purpose, and the cell has more than one response route.

Murai 2012 compared niraparib, olaparib and veliparib in defined cellular and biochemical systems: niraparib and olaparib trapped PARP-DNA complexes more strongly than veliparib, despite catalytic inhibition being a different comparison. Murai 2014 compared BMN673, now talazoparib, with olaparib and rucaparib. In damaged-DNA cell assays, 0.1 micromolar BMN673 produced a trapping signal comparable to 10 micromolar olaparib, about a 100-fold concentration difference; the purified DNA-binding assay gave a different, roughly 40-fold comparison. Similar catalytic effects did not imply similar trapping. Strongest among compounds tested in 2014 is not a ranking of clinical benefit, tolerated exposure or personal treatment choices.

A DNA-associated protein obstacle can challenge copying without every encounter becoming a measured collision, double-strand break or cell death. Farmer 2005 demonstrated increased sensitivity to PARP inhibition in experimental BRCA-deficient systems. Cong 2021 studied single-stranded replication gaps in cellular models: gap suppression tracked resistance or resensitisation, while restoring fork protection did not always restore resistance in the tested models. Obstacle and gap explanations can coexist, but their relative contribution in a patient's tumour is not established by these experiments. A repair-gene variant alone does not reproduce the functional losses tested in a synthetic-lethal experiment.

Two schematic pictures ask different questions. Matched snapshots of DNA-bound PARP1 with a longer or shorter PAR chain illustrate catalytic output; a generic inhibitor in the catalytic pocket does not measure binding duration. A second picture places approaching copying machinery behind a retained PARP1 complex, with visible separation; it does not show an observed collision, literal backbone conformation or a measured effect size. Reduced catalytic activity and DNA retention can occur together. The arrows therefore lead to further context-dependent measurements, rather than two independent proofs of a clinical mechanism or a drug ranking.

Enzyme assays and PAR immunoassays report catalytic activity or its product. NCI's PAR assay measures PAR levels in specified biospecimens; chromatin-associated PARP measurements instead investigate DNA retention under specified conditions. Repair readouts and survival/regrowth experiments add other information. Murai's experiments used defined cell lines, DNA damage and drug concentrations, so neither a reduced metabolic or ATP signal alone nor a picture establishes irreversible death or its cause. Matched genetic perturbations and appropriate controls are needed to distinguish reduced growth, reduced metabolism and loss of long-term survival.

Waks's selected resistant breast cancer cohort illustrates why historical repair markers and current repair can diverge: four definite or putative BRCA reversion cases acquired RAD51 foci, and other proposed routes included 53BP1 loss and MRE11A amplification. The 53BP1-loss case lacked enough tissue for direct functional confirmation. A historical scar or sequence hypothesis cannot establish a present PARP vulnerability, and this small cohort does not supply an all-patient resistance rule. Biological plausibility, a qualifying label indication and a trial place are separate requirements.

For example, the U.S. olaparib label effective July 2025 specifies adjuvant treatment of adults with deleterious or suspected-deleterious germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer after neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, selected with an approved companion diagnostic. A tumour-only BRCA result or high scar score cannot replace the germline and disease-setting requirements. That indication does not establish that a different PARP inhibitor, a different setting or a plausible mechanism has the same approval or access conditions.

In a fictional comparison, compounds A and B inhibit PARP catalytic activity similarly, but A retains more PARP on DNA in a culture assay. The conclusion is an assay-specific trapping difference. Useful exposure, survival, safety, resistance and clinical outcomes still need evidence. More trapping in that system does not establish a better treatment, and neither an old scar nor a repair-gene name identifies which effect matters in the current tumour.

Hoslett and colleagues' 2026 preclinical study investigated selective disposal of trapped PARP1 involving TEX264, the protein-remodelling enzyme p97 and LC3-associated lysosomal handling. Autophagic handling of nuclear material is called nucleophagy. Perturbing the machinery increased chromatin-associated PARP1 and PARP-inhibitor sensitivity in the studied systems; complementation and cargo-recognition experiments supported the proposed route. Some trapping experiments also supplied the DNA-damaging agent MMS, so their conditions are not every drug-alone exposure. The authors left the exact export or packaging of nuclear cargo, and macroautophagy versus direct microautophagy, unresolved. A clearance cartoon is therefore a mechanistic model, not established compartment geometry. Expression-survival associations do not validate TEX264 expression as a treatment-response test.

In a fictional culture, more death with a PARP inhibitor plus a lysosomal drug fits several explanations: reduced clearance of trapped PARP, toxicity from the second drug itself, or another altered stress response. Measure chromatin-bound PARP1 over the relevant interval, include both single-drug conditions, and test the proposed clearance machinery with suitable independent perturbation and restoration. Unchanged trapped cargo despite more death argues against that particular clearance explanation. TEX264 or p97 perturbation is complementary evidence, not automatically perfectly selective, because proteins can have other functions. Chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine alter lysosomal processes broadly. Survival alone, high recycling RNA or a broad lysosomal effect does not identify selective trapped-PARP disposal or establish patient benefit.

records.name: Phosphorylation
records.tldr: Adding phosphate can change a protein’s behavior in several ways. The site and cellular context determine whether a measured change indicates activation, inhibition or something else.
records.summary: Protein kinases commonly transfer phosphate from ATP to a substrate, producing ADP. Protein phosphatases remove phosphate by hydrolysis without regenerating ATP. A modification can affect catalysis, binding, localization or interactions; sites on one protein can have different functions. Src experiments demonstrated an inhibitory tail-phosphorylation mechanism in their defined preparation, so phosphorylation should not be treated as universal activation.

records.name: PI3K / AKT / mTOR
records.tldr: This network links growth signals and nutrients to protein production, metabolism and recycling. Different branches can respond differently to an intervention.
records.summary:
Class I PI3K phosphorylates a membrane lipid, producing PIP3; PTEN removes its position-3 phosphate. AKT and mTOR are protein kinases. A PIP3 lipid result and an AKT1 Ser473 phosphosite result are therefore different molecular measurements. Document specimen preservation, cell mixture, protein site, timing, exposure, comparator and total-protein normalization before interpreting a change as activity or dependence.

Membrane recruitment helps organize AKT activation. PDK1 phosphorylates AKT1 Thr308, whereas the rictor-mTOR complex supplies Ser473 phosphorylation in the defined experimental route. AKT can inhibit TSC2, relieving the TSC1/2 brake on RHEB, which promotes mTORC1 signaling. The diagram's indirect AKT-to-mTORC1 connection stands for these regulatory steps; it is not direct phosphorylation of mTORC1 by AKT.

Raptor-containing mTORC1 and rictor-containing mTORC2 are distinct complexes. mTORC1 regulates protein production and autophagy-initiation machinery; releasing initiation restraint is not proof of completed recycling flux. Harrington linked S6K activity to reduced IRS-1 function, and O'Reilly observed increased IRS-1 and AKT signaling after RAD001 in cell models and treated tumors. Feedback release can change an output without proving that a combination improves outcomes in every setting.

In a fictional mTORC1 perturbation, lower production-regulator phosphorylation followed by higher AKT1 Ser473 and unchanged growth supports biochemical changes, not essentiality or failed engagement; timing alone does not prove the feedback connection. Test the proposed wiring and functional outcome independently. records.name: RNA
records.tldr: RNA is a family of molecules with several jobs. Messenger RNA provides a protein-making template; other RNAs help build, regulate or carry out cellular processes.
records.summary: RNA uses ribose and usually uracil in place of DNA’s thymine. It is often single-stranded but can fold through internal pairing. Messenger RNA carries a coding template; ribosomal RNA contributes to ribosome structure and catalysis; transfer RNA brings amino acids; regulatory RNAs influence other molecules. Many nuclear messages receive a 5-prime cap and poly(A) tail and have introns removed by splicing before translation, but these features are not universal to all RNAs. Ribosomes read a coding sequence in codons to produce a polypeptide; processing, folding and localization follow.

records.name: Receptor tyrosine kinase activation
records.tldr: Receptor tyrosine kinases can relay signals from outside a cell through protein phosphorylation. Receptor amount, signalling, drug binding and growth dependence are different measurements.
records.summary:
EGFR, FGFR and FLT3 are examples of receptor tyrosine kinases. Their normal roles and activation arrangements differ across receptor families.

Receptor amount, phosphorylation, direct drug engagement, growth dependence and clinical benefit are separate observations. Lower receptor phosphorylation supports a biochemical effect under the assay conditions but can also reflect indirect regulation; it does not by itself prove direct binding. A controlled functional effect with independent specificity tests is needed before assigning receptor dependence.

Many RTKs have extracellular ligand-binding regions, membrane-spanning regions and intracellular tyrosine-kinase machinery. Families activate differently: Zhang demonstrated an asymmetric EGFR kinase-domain interaction, while Stauber examined an FGF1-FGFR2 extracellular complex with a proposed heparin-related assembly arrangement. Ligand, helper molecules, receptor member and context matter. A downstream phosphosite can have multiple upstream causes and is not a universal receptor meter.

Slamon 1987 studied 189 primary breast cancers and reported HER2 amplification in 30%, associated with relapse and survival; that historical study is not a present-day universal prevalence or a causal drug-response experiment. In the 2001 randomized trial of 469 women with HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer, adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy increased median survival from 20.3 to 25.1 months, with cardiac toxicity as a material risk. A trial median summarizes a group and does not predict an individual survival time.

In a fictional comparison, two cultures contain a receptor, but only the amplified, high-surface-protein culture slows growth after a blocking antibody, while receptor phosphorylation falls in both. This separates amount, sampled signaling and growth response; the pattern suggests dependence but attribution still needs controls and independent perturbation. RNA is not surface accessibility, a family-name inhibitor need not engage every member at the tested exposure. For an antibody-drug conjugate, receptor access and payload delivery are separate questions from whether growth requires that receptor's signaling. Fixed-tissue staining and viable-model perturbation have different input costs and validation scopes.

records.name: Cellular senescence
records.tldr: Senescent cells remain alive while their division is durably arrested. Their effects depend on the cells, signals and surrounding tissue.
records.summary: Senescence is a stress-associated cell state with durable cell-cycle arrest and other context-dependent features. Identifying it requires combined measurements rather than one marker. In genetically switchable blood-cancer models, release from senescence allowed renewed division with enhanced clonogenic potential. That experimental result does not predict that every senescent cell will restart or that a person will relapse. Arrest, secretion and effects on neighbouring cells require separate assessment. Model findings do not establish a preferred senolytic treatment.

records.name: Single-cell mass and growth-rate assays
records.tldr: Repeated calibrated mass measurements can estimate a cell's growth rate; slower mass accumulation does not by itself show cell death.
records.summary: A suspended microchannel resonator weighs a cell relative to the fluid it displaces using the shift in a vibrating beam's frequency. Buoyant mass equals cell volume multiplied by the difference between cell and fluid density. It is not simply diameter or dry mass. Repeatedly measuring the same cell estimates mass accumulation rate; Godin reversed the flow to reintroduce the same cell to the sensor (a dynamic trap) and Cermak used serial sensors along one channel. Stevens investigated drug-response associations in specified cancer models and leukaemia samples, rather than universal clinical prediction.

Tracking repeated readings estimates a slope, often picograms per hour; mass-normalised rates have inverse-time units. Preparation and exposure consume finite material; the physical measurement can preserve cells, but recovery and downstream compatibility depend on the method.

Quality and inference. Check clumps, cell attribution, instrument drift, calibration, tracking ambiguity and sufficient linked readings. Serial-sensor analyses exclude uncertain matches rather than invent a trajectory. Fluid-density changes can change buoyant mass. A small positive slope still indicates accumulation in the observed interval; later recovery, death and resistance need additional endpoints and time. Many measured cells from one specimen are not many independent patients. No universal rate cutoff establishes clinical sensitivity or immune recognition. Buoyant mass is also not a count of cell divisions. Physical measurement performance, a reproducible drug-response association and validated use for a clinical decision are separate kinds of evidence. Without extra measurements or assumptions, this sensor does not establish dry mass, a death mechanism, immune specificity or patient benefit.

Fictional arithmetic. A tracked cell rising from 10 to 12 picograms over one hour has a slope of 2 picograms per hour. Comparable groups at 2 and 0.5 picograms per hour differ by (2 minus 0.5) divided by 2, or 75 percent. Both rates are positive. The positive research use is a rapid physical response readout and a view of cell-to-cell variation that a population average can conceal. records.name: Synthetic lethality
records.tldr: Synthetic lethality means that two impairments together kill a cell even though either alone is tolerated; finding one genetic change does not establish that a particular drug will produce that interaction.
records.summary:
Synthetic lethality is a lethal interaction between two impairments, each of which can be tolerated alone in the tested system. One impairment may already be present in a cancer and an experimental intervention can create the second, so the concept does not require two drugs. Genetic identity, loss of function, target engagement and the lethal outcome each need evidence.

The 2005 Farmer and Bryant studies found sensitivity to PARP inhibition in BRCA-impaired experimental systems. Murai and colleagues later distinguished PARP trapping from catalytic inhibition. These findings support particular mechanisms; they do not make every BRCA-related finding a clinical selection rule. Candidate pairs such as MTAP with PRMT5, mismatch-repair deficiency with WRN, or repair deficiency with POLQ need their own model, exposure, selectivity and clinical evidence.

Measure death separately from slower growth, because a viability signal can fall when cells divide less or change metabolism; pair a suitable death assay with long-term survival or colony formation, and record concentration, time and denominator, remembering that colony formation measures reproductive survival and not the way cells die. Synthetic lethality is not oncogene addiction, which is dependence on an active driver: in Src-, BCR-ABL- and EGF receptor-dependent cells, unequal attenuation of survival and pro-apoptotic signals after the driver is inactivated contributes to death (Sharma et al.). It is also not synergy, since a score above a reference model does not identify which losses interact. In the BRCA/PARP example, homologous recombination is a DNA repair process and HRD means deficiency of that process. Trapping PARP on DNA and inhibiting its catalytic activity are different perturbations, while repair restoration or changes in replication stress can change sensitivity. The first impairment can pre-exist, so a two-loss interaction does not require two drugs.

Rescue, restoration and what each test can show. A rescue experiment restores a relevant function and asks whether the predicted harm falls; that strengthens attribution, but a failed rescue is not automatic disproof, because the restored function may not be expressed, localised or timed adequately (a reading rule, not a result from these experiments). A real example of functional restoration involved secondary BRCA2 mutations, often described as reversions. Ovarian cancer lines PEO1, PEO4 and PEO6 came from one BRCA2 mutation carrier: PEO1 was BRCA2 deficient and sensitive to cisplatin and a PARP inhibitor, while a secondary BRCA2 mutation that cancelled the inherited one arose in the patient (PEO4, PEO6) and, under cisplatin and PARP-inhibitor selection of PEO1, in the dish, restoring BRCA2 and resistance. Function was shown by homologous recombination assays after transfecting wild-type or mutant BRCA2 cDNA into reporter cells, and transient siRNA depletion (two siRNAs against a non-targeting control) re-sensitised the restored clones and PEO4 (Sakai et al. 2009). Normal tissue can share the vulnerability: normal Brca2-deficient mouse intestinal epithelium showed very high apoptosis within hours of PARP inhibition (Hay et al.). None of this establishes clinical benefit.

A fictional test uses matched cultures over the same interval: neither impairment, A alone, B alone and A plus B. Each single impairment is tolerated and only the pair causes death measured by a validated assay, with independent perturbations reproducing it. In a separate rescue culture, restoring A while B remains impaired reduces death; this tests attribution and does not revive already dead cells. If a short assay instead shows fewer cells, slower division and cell loss remain unresolved. Other cell backgrounds and normal cells are separate tests of context and selectivity.

records.name: Ubiquitin-proteasome system & protein homeostasis
records.tldr: Ubiquitin can change a protein's interactions, location or fate. Some tags support proteasomal destruction; tagging alone does not establish completed degradation.
records.summary: E1 enzymes activate ubiquitin, E2 enzymes carry it and E3 ligases help select substrates and assemble modifications. Chain architecture and cellular context influence the result; ubiquitination is not universally a destruction signal. Deubiquitinases can remove or remodel tags, and proteasomal degradation is a later process that needs its own evidence. A protein can fall because synthesis changes, cells are lost or degradation increases, so abundance alone does not identify the route. In targeted-degradation experiments, target binding, E3 recruitment, protein loss, proteasome dependence and sustained cellular effects are distinct observations. Proteasome inhibitors and recruited-degradation strategies intervene at different steps; mechanistic measurements do not by themselves establish clinical benefit.

notes: Ubiquitin is a small protein attached through enzyme steps: E1 uses ATP for activation, E2 carries activated ubiquitin, and E3 promotes substrate selection and transfer. Reticulocyte experiments separated these functions. E3 families differ in transfer mechanism; no single cartoon specifies all of them.

Suitable tagged cargo can be unfolded by ATP-dependent proteasomal machinery and broken into fragments, while ubiquitin is removed and reused. Other ubiquitin signals organise interactions rather than destruction, and yeast experiments show overlapping chain functions. Lysosomal autophagy and proteasomal breakdown are distinct routes.

Protein abundance reflects synthesis and removal. Measure named-substrate decay over time with synthesis, handling and viability controls; restoration of an E3 adaptor can strengthen attribution without proving direct binding or global proteasome failure. Catalytic activity per time, ubiquitinated-cargo intensity and protein lifetime in hours are different readouts. KEAP1 is one CUL3 adaptor for NRF2, so a CUL3 change cannot uniquely identify that substrate. Pulse labelling or a controlled temporary synthesis block can help estimate turnover but may cause stress. Independent perturbation and restoration help distinguish a selected-substrate effect from a secondary response; enzyme engagement alone does not establish selective killing.

In a randomised trial of 669 people with relapsed myeloma after one to three prior therapies, bortezomib prolonged median time to progression compared with high-dose dexamethasone: 6.22 versus 3.49 months. This historical clinical result does not make an arbitrary E3 variant or abundant protein a predictive treatment biomarker.

Proteasomal degradation commonly handles individual suitable proteins, whereas lysosomal macroautophagy can deliver aggregates, organelles and portions of cytoplasm. This is a distinction of machinery and typical cargo, not an absolute partition: ubiquitinated material can also be recognised by autophagy adaptors such as p62. A tagged protein, an autophagic membrane marker and disappearance of a named cargo are different observations. Bortezomib's relapsed-myeloma trial result does not predict a hydroxychloroquine result in pancreatic cancer, and blocking both routes does not by itself demonstrate selective harm to malignant cells.
records.analogy: A recycling plant with barcode stickers (ubiquitin) and a shredder (proteasome). Myeloma is a paper mill that produces so much waste it dies when the shredder stops (bortezomib). PROTACs and glues are forged stickers that get the plant to shred the cancer's own machinery.

records.name: Variant allele frequency (VAF)
records.tldr: Variant allele frequency is the fraction of informative reads or molecules that support a variant under a test’s definition. It is not directly the fraction of cancer cells.
records.summary: Read-based VAF divides variant-supporting reads by informative reads at the locus. Some assays instead report a molecule-based measure, so keep the laboratory’s definition. Tumor purity, local allele-specific copy number, ploidy, subclonal mixture and assay behavior affect the value. VAF alone cannot assign zygosity, variant origin, the number of clones or a cancer-cell percentage. Changes over time in plasma also require attention to specimen and non-tumor DNA contributors.

notes: VAF is the proportion of usable reads or assay-defined molecules supporting the alternate sequence; keep the denominator: 25 of 100 usable observations is 25%.

CCF is carrier cancer cells over all sampled cancer cells; its inputs have distinct denominators: cell purity p, DNA contribution, pathology cellularity (method-defined, for RCB the tumour-bed area), global ploidy P, local copy number C, mutant multiplicity m.
With equal recovery per genome copy and diploid normals, tumour DNA contribution is p*P/[p*P+2*(1-p)]; half the cells at ploidy four contribute two thirds of DNA.

For uniform local copies, expected VAF is p*f*m/[p*C+(1-p)*2]; assumptions: two normal copies, uniform cancer copies, fixed multiplicity, unbiased observations; subclonal copy change needs a richer model.
Same 50 cancer plus 50 normal cells, every cancer cell carrying one variant copy: expected VAF 50/200=25% with two local cancer copies and 50/150 about 33% with one; CCF stays 100% and purity 50%.

Purity 0.5, one mutant copy: four local copies with CCF 100% and two local copies with CCF 2/3 both predict VAF 1/6 (about 16.7%); copy evidence separates them; CCF above 100% signals incompatible assumptions.

High VAF alone cannot establish truncal ancestry or origin or function; a rise after treatment can reflect mixture or copy change as well as carrier expansion; uncertain inputs give alternative CCF fits, not counted cells.

Retain DNA and copy-state inputs, filtered support denominators, fractions, local copies, multiplicity, purity, model version and alternative fits. New extraction consumes material; reanalysis alone does not. Artifacts, few molecules, recovery bias and uncertain copy/mixture estimates limit conversion. Detection thresholds and model-fit criteria do not establish a universal clonal-target cutoff or treatment benefit.

Fictional splice-site example: 32 alternate reads among 160 usable reads give VAF 20 per cent. Suppose half the sampled cells are malignant, every cell has two local copies, and each affected cancer cell carries one altered copy, with equal recovery per copy. Then VAF = purity times cancer-cell fraction divided by two; 0.20 = 0.50 times CCF divided by two gives CCF 80 per cent. With pure cancer-cell input, the same 20 per cent fits CCF 40 per cent. These are model calculations, not counted cells. Local copy changes, altered-copy multiplicity, recovery bias or uncertain purity can change the fit. A measured splice junction and functional repair remain separate questions.

records.name: Variant calling
records.tldr: Variant calling evaluates sequence evidence and error models to identify candidate changes within a defined assay scope.
records.summary: Variant calling assesses whether observed sequence or regional evidence supports a difference from a reference or comparison sample. Evidence quality, independent fragments, local depth, error models and the alteration class matter. Annotation describes possible consequence after calling; neither annotation nor a passed filter independently proves function or treatment relevance. Negative calls retain the workflow coverage and detection limits.

notes: Base quality concerns confidence in a sequence letter; mapping quality concerns its proposed location. A clear letter can still map ambiguously. Depth depends on the chosen quality, duplicate and overlapping-pair filters, so retain these rules with support counts. Source: https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools-depth.html, samtools 1.25 manual.

Passing a computational filter does not establish biological function or treatment benefit. Agreement between callers using the same reads does not create independent molecular evidence; a shared mapping problem can remain. The exact regions, alteration classes and usable local evidence constrain a negative result.

Variant calling evaluates sequence evidence and error models to identify candidate differences; methods are class-specific (substitutions, indels, copy changes, rearrangements) and a workflow calling one class may not call another.
Evidence includes usable depth, base and mapping quality, strand and fragment distribution and comparison-sample support; somatic callers must handle low-frequency evidence in mixed samples.
In VCF, PASS means the call passed the stated filters; a dot means filters have not been applied; counts and allele fractions need defined denominators.
Annotation adds gene or predicted consequence and is separate from calling; machine learning is one method, not the definition.
Two callers agreeing on shared reads can share misalignment error; confirmation needs an independent suitable method; a negative call set is bounded by detectable regions, classes and fractions.
Fictional teaching exercise: A call that is PASS in two tools but supported only by reads aligning ambiguously to duplicated regions has not resolved location.

Calling uses existing reads, a reference assembly and optional comparison files; a new confirmation assay can consume more material. Report coordinates, alleles, support, quality, filters and defined fractions/copy estimates. Retain caller version, detectable regions/classes and thresholds. Contamination, damage, misalignment and reference mismatch require specimen-specific end-to-end validation; filter thresholds are not treatment thresholds.

A confirmation should test the suspected weakness. Check specimen identity and tissue, preparation, alteration class, usable local coverage, read quality and alignment; a high average depth does not establish adequate evidence at the disputed site. Reformatting one call or rerunning the same reads does not create independent molecular evidence. A separate preparation or a method with different relevant failure modes may help; a different brand name alone does not establish independence. In a fictional comparison, assay A reports a low-fraction variant and B reports none without site coverage. B has not disproved A. Request the exact site, usable local support, class-specific detection limit, specimen and time point. If both tests were adequate, reconcile the discrepancy, including sampling different populations or times, before building further interpretations.

Paired tumour and an appropriate nonmalignant comparator help attribute a finding. Jones and colleagues' 2015 paired analyses showed why tumour-only interpretation can misclassify inherited findings. The normal comparator also needs adequate evidence at the site. In a fictional repair-gene example, 32 alternate reads among 160 usable reads give a 20 per cent observed fraction; an adequate matched normal lacking the change supports somatic origin in those sampled tissues. Neither that attribution nor a second adequate confirmation establishes that the change drives the cancer, disrupts repair or predicts treatment response. A familiar gene and a credible sequence call answer different questions from measured RNA, protein function and clinical actionability.

records.name: Variant effect prediction
records.tldr: A variant-effect prediction estimates a defined consequence of a DNA change for a specified transcript or task. It does not by itself establish disease causation or treatment benefit.
records.summary: Variant-effect prediction estimates a specified consequence of a sequence change, whereas variant calling identifies changes from sequence data. Ensembl maps each allele of a variant onto every overlapping transcript with a rule-based approach, so the same genomic change can have a different consequence in different transcripts, and its impact categories (high, moderate, low, modifier) are qualitative assumptions about likely effect, not a measured loss of function (Ensembl documentation, release 116). A score from a missense tool does not answer a splice or regulatory question, and a prediction should name the reference genome, the alleles and the transcript (with its version) it was made for. A raw model score is not automatically a probability: a splice score of 0.92 on an unspecified scale does not mean a 92 per cent chance of lost function, because thresholds and evidence strengths belong to a particular tool and task. The absence of a prediction does not make a variant benign, because a tool may not cover that variant type or transcript. RNA junction evidence, functional experiments and clinical studies address different gaps, and none is interchangeable with a sequence score. Two reports of the same prediction from the same software version are two copies of one computed result, not two independent experiments. Where a tool's training data overlap the variants used to evaluate it, its performance can be overestimated, which is why the ClinGen calibration of thirteen missense tools to ACMG/AMP pathogenicity and benignity evidence strengths, estimated from local positive predictive value, used datasets assembled to minimise that circularity (Pejaver and colleagues, 2022). That calibration used ClinVar missense variants classified as pathogenic or benign and rare in gnomAD, within the ACMG/AMP recommendations for variants in genes associated with monogenic disease, and it selected no tool designed for splice variants. Its introduction notes that many methods overlap and so do not offer independent assessment of pathogenicity, which is why agreement between tools that share training data or inputs is not independent confirmation. The AMP, ASCO and CAP guideline for somatic variants notes that early prediction algorithms were developed and validated for germline variants and recommends that their results never be used as the sole evidence for variant classification or clinical decision making (Li and colleagues, 2017).

notes: Model card for a variant-effect tool (a reading guide, not a score). Measures: a predicted consequence or effect for a stated sequence change and task. How: confirm the input change, choose the reference and model, calculate the output, then interpret it against calibration that suits the task. Input and tissue cost: existing sequence data and reference metadata; the computation uses no tissue, although producing the sequence input may have consumed a specimen. Output and units: consequence terms or model-specific scores, with tool version and transcript. Thresholds: tool-, task- and validation-specific, with no universal damaging cutoff. Failure modes: wrong transcript, unsupported variant type, biased evaluation or incompatible inputs. Cannot establish alone: measured protein function, a complete tumour mechanism or benefit from a drug. Validation tier: a software output has no automatic clinical status; the laboratory's validated intended use is a separate question.

Figure reading (fictional layouts, no real coordinates): one genomic change, labelled P (C to T), falls inside an exon of transcript T1 and inside an intron of transcript T2 because the two transcripts have different exon boundaries. Three separate questions follow: annotation asks where P sits, a splice model asks whether exon joining could change, and an RNA assay tests the proposed joins. A score needs its model's task and scale, and a predicted effect does not establish benefit.

records.name: Variant of uncertain significance (VUS)
records.tldr: A variant of uncertain significance (VUS) is a genetic change that has been found but nobody yet knows whether it matters.
records.summary: A variant of uncertain significance (VUS) is a genetic change that has been detected but whose effect on disease is not yet known. Such findings are common on germline panels and in tumour sequencing, and they should not drive treatment decisions; over time many are reclassified through ClinVar, functional assays and population data. The term is linked to the Germline (hereditary) testing and Comprehensive genomic profiling technologies, to the ClinVar collection and AlphaMissense, and to the terms Mutation, Genomic profiling and Hereditary cancer syndromes. It appears in the bottleneck on unidentified inherited risk, and ideas that respond to it include testing every possible mutation in every cancer gene so no result is uncertain, and a plain-language version of every genomic report.

records.name: Warburg effect
records.tldr: The Warburg effect is a pattern of making lactate from glucose while oxygen is available. It does not mean that mitochondrial energy production has stopped.
records.summary: Aerobic glycolysis can coexist with mitochondrial glucose oxidation and use of other nutrients. Human lung-tumour tracer experiments demonstrated variation within and between tumours, rather than a single cancer-wide metabolic state. The pattern can support proliferation but does not establish an irreplaceable survival requirement. Glucose uptake, lactate release, oxygen consumption and calculated energy production answer different questions. Neither this pattern nor a culture nutrient-removal result supplies a dietary or drug recommendation.

notes: The Warburg effect describes substantial glucose-to-lactate metabolism with oxygen available. Glycolysis can supply ATP and lactate formation regenerates a carrier needed for its continuation. Lactate production does not imply absent mitochondrial oxidation, and proliferating normal cells can use aerobic glycolysis too.

Intraoperative glucose-tracer studies in nine people with non-small-cell lung cancer found enhanced glycolysis alongside glucose oxidation, with heterogeneity within and between tumours and evidence for other nutrient use. These observations do not describe every cancer or establish an irreplaceable survival route.

FDG imaging measures uptake and trapping of a glucose analogue, not lactate production or a cancer-exclusive process. Respiratory carbon dioxide contributes to medium acidification, so pH change is not pure glycolysis. Keep oxygen conditions, viable-cell normalisation, tracer identity, metabolites and timing with rate measurements; tracer labelling alone is not automatically a complete flux estimate.

Lactate release, oxygen consumption and labelled glucose reaching mitochondrial metabolites can coexist. High pathway activity, a transcript signature or glucose uptake does not prove survival dependence. A culture nutrient-removal experiment does not establish that changing a person's diet selectively starves a tumour or identifies a medicine. Functional rate or tracer studies use viable cells, slices or a defined in-vivo experiment and consume or perturb material. No universal Warburg-positive threshold predicts treatment benefit; a functional perturbation and survival outcome are separate from the metabolic pattern.

records.name: Wnt / β-catenin
records.tldr: Canonical Wnt signalling regulates beta-catenin and gene activity. Its output, dependence on a Wnt ligand and effects on cell growth are separate questions.
records.summary:
Canonical pathway output, dependence on secreted Wnt, growth dependence and clinical response are separate claims. Nuclear beta-catenin can reflect pathway signaling, whereas total beta-catenin also includes adhesion functions. Lower AXIN2 RNA supports an output effect with suitable controls, not selective killing or patient benefit. Wnt routes that do not use beta-catenin are outside this canonical readout.

Canonical Wnt uses Frizzled with LRP5/6 co-receptor machinery. Without an effective signal, the Axin/APC-organized destruction machinery and sequential kinase steps promote beta-catenin degradation; signaling can change that control and allow nuclear regulation with partners. PORCN supplies a lipid modification required for proper Wnt secretion in the studied systems. Blocking that upstream step need not overcome a downstream escape from destruction control.

Two fictional cultures have nuclear beta-catenin. Secretion blockade reduces the nuclear signal in culture A but not in culture B, where downstream bypass is stipulated. A supports a ligand-dependent hypothesis; B illustrates how an upstream block can leave a downstream output intact. The symbols represent qualitative readouts, not protein counts or a real drug dataset. Neither pattern alone establishes selective killing; measure viability and control intervention specificity.

Assays can measure localization, AXIN2 RNA or a defined transcriptional reporter, before and after a specified perturbation. Preservation, composition, global transcription effects, model validation and tissue consumption matter; there is no universal Wnt-high treatment cutoff. In Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study of 94 people with advanced solid tumors, AXIN2 fell in many paired biopsies while no RECIST responses were observed. Target-related output and tumor response must therefore be reported separately, alongside safety rather than a claim of demonstrated benefit.

Rodon's phase 1 WNT974 study treated 94 people with advanced solid tumours. AXIN2 RNA decreased in 94 per cent of 52 paired skin-biopsy comparisons and 74 per cent of 35 paired tumour-biopsy comparisons; no RECIST responses were observed. These denominators are paired-sample groups, not response fractions out of all 94 participants. A downstream output change supports a pharmacodynamic effect without directly measuring receptor occupancy, selective growth dependence or tumour shrinkage. Dysgeusia occurred in 50 per cent, illustrating that normal-tissue effects also matter. This trial does not justify transferring a target-output change to benefit or a treatment recommendation.
